records.title: 2.4L Tigershark Excessive Oil Consumption
records.description: The 2.4L Tigershark MultiAir four-cylinder consumes excessive oil, with owners reporting roughly one quart every 1,000 miles. The cause is attributed to low-tension piston rings that don't seal properly against the cylinder walls, allowing oil to be burned in the combustion chamber. Because the low-oil warning may not illuminate until oil is critically low, the engine can stall or suffer accelerated wear, which led to a class-action settlement covering 2.4L FCA engines.
records.solution: Dealers reprogram the PCM (and TCM) to monitor oil level/consumption, then perform a documented oil-consumption test; if consumption exceeds about one quart per 2,000 miles, a long-block/engine replacement is authorized. Affected owners may qualify under the Tigershark oil-consumption settlement. Out of coverage, check oil frequently and budget for ring/engine repair.
symptoms: Burning roughly 1 quart of oil per 1,000 miles
Possible stalling when oil runs low

citations.title: FCA Bulletin 09-018-24 - 2.4L Excessive Oil Consumption XB1 Warranty Extension

records.title: 62TE 6-Speed Transmission Failure (Gen 1)
records.description: The first-generation Chrysler 200 (rebadged Sebring) uses the 62TE 6-speed automatic which suffers from solenoid pack failures, valve body issues, and worn sealing rings. Hard shifting, slipping, and complete failure are common, often before 100,000 miles.
records.solution: Solenoid pack replacement (68376696AA) for early symptoms. Full transmission rebuild or replacement for severe cases. Use ONLY Mopar ATF+4 fluid (68218058AC). Change fluid every 30,000 miles.
symptoms: Hard shifting or jerking between gears

records.title: ZF 9-Speed Transmission Shifting Problems
records.description: The ZF 9HP48 9-speed automatic transmission suffers from harsh shifting, delayed engagement, lurching forward, and unexpectedly shifting into neutral while driving. A terminal crimping issue in sensor cluster harness assemblies caused wiring defects. 2015 models are worst; 2016+ have improvements after FCA built transmissions in Kokomo, Indiana. Recall S55 (NHTSA 16V529000) issued.
records.solution: Contact dealer for Recall S55 (NHTSA 16V529000) - provides free PCM/TCM reprogramming and transaxle range sensor wire harness replacement if needed. If ordering 2015 replacement transmission, the system automatically provides improved 2016 unit. Regular transmission fluid services every 60,000 miles.
symptoms: Delayed engagement when shifting from Park

records.title: A/C Evaporator Core Leak
records.description: The A/C evaporator core develops pinhole leaks from corrosion, causing a gradual loss of refrigerant and diminished cooling performance. The evaporator is located inside the HVAC housing behind the dashboard, making it a labor-intensive repair. Moisture and debris accumulation on the evaporator surface accelerate corrosion. The refrigerant leak rate is often slow enough that the A/C loses effectiveness over weeks to months rather than failing suddenly.
records.solution: Replace the A/C evaporator core. This is a major repair requiring partial dashboard removal to access the HVAC housing. The evaporator, expansion valve, and receiver/drier should all be replaced together. The system must then be evacuated and recharged with R-134a refrigerant (2011-2014) or R-1234yf (2015-2017). Budget $800-$1,500 for the complete repair due to labor intensity.
symptoms: A/C gradually loses cooling effectiveness over weeks
Musty or sweet smell from dashboard vents
A/C cycles on and off frequently
Wet carpet on passenger side from condensate overflow
Need to recharge A/C more than once per year

records.title: Cruise Control Cannot Be Cancelled
records.description: A wiring short circuit can prevent the cruise control from being cancelled, so the vehicle may not slow when the brake is tapped or the system is switched off, and could maintain speed or accelerate. The 200 was part of FCA's huge May 2018 recall of about 4.8 million vehicles. NHTSA recall 18V-332 covers 2015-2017 Chrysler 200 models among many other FCA vehicles.
records.solution: Under recall U59 / NHTSA 18V-332, dealers reflash the powertrain/engine control module software free of charge. Until repaired, FCA advised against using cruise control; if it can't be cancelled while driving, firmly apply the brakes, shift to neutral, then park once stopped.
symptoms: Cruise control will not disengage with brake pedal
Cruise control will not turn off via the switch
Vehicle holds speed or accelerates with cruise engaged

citations.title: FCA Safety Recall U59 / NHTSA 18V-332 - Reprogram Powertrain Control Module

records.title: Parasitic Battery Drain - Modules Not Sleeping
records.description: The second-generation 200 suffers from parasitic battery drain caused by modules not going to sleep properly. The Body Control Module and UConnect system are common culprits. Battery can die in 2-3 days of sitting.
records.solution: Request latest BCM software update from dealer. Check for aftermarket accessories causing draw. Disconnect negative battery terminal if parking for more than 3 days. Replace battery with AGM type for better cold-weather performance.
symptoms: Interior lights staying on after exiting
Door lock/unlock cycling on its own

records.title: First-Generation Engine Stalling at Low Speed / Idle
records.description: First-generation 200s stall without warning during low-speed deceleration, such as braking for a stop sign or while idling. NHTSA opened preliminary investigation PE12-016 in June 2012 covering an estimated 87,288 vehicles after the PCM was found to run a fuel-vapor purge monitor at idle/decel, creating an overly rich condition that killed the engine. A software 'customer satisfaction' update followed, but complaints persisted; FCA later found a damaged connector in the fuse/relay box and recalled about 85,000 sedans in 2015.
records.solution: Apply the FCA PCM software update from the original customer-satisfaction program. For continued stalling, inspect and replace the damaged fuse/relay-box connector per the 2015 recall. A failing crankshaft/camshaft sensor or wiring should also be checked if codes are present.
symptoms: Engine stalls without warning when slowing/braking
Loss of power steering and brake assist after stall

citations.title: NHTSA PE12-016 Closing Resume - 2011 Chrysler 200 Engine Stall

records.title: 2.4L Tigershark Excessive Oil Consumption
records.description: The 2.4L Tigershark MultiAir II engine has defective piston rings that allow oil into the combustion chamber. Owners report consuming 1 quart of oil every 500-1,000 miles. Engine can seize without warning if oil drops too low. Class-action settlement (Wood, et al. v. FCA US, LLC) reached. FCA extended powertrain warranty to 7 years/100,000 miles under CSN W80.
records.solution: Contact FCA dealer for oil consumption test under CSN W80 warranty extension. If test fails, engine long block replacement under extended warranty (7 years/100,000 miles). PCM/TCM reprogramming may reduce consumption in some cases. File claim at fcatigersharksettlement.com if eligible. Use full synthetic 0W-20 oil.
symptoms: Oil consumption of 1+ quart per 1,000 miles
Engine stalling or seizing without warning

records.title: Oil Filter Housing / Cooler Leak (2.4L Tigershark)
records.description: The oil filter housing and integrated oil cooler on the 2.4L Tigershark engine develops leaks from the housing gasket and the oil cooler O-rings. Oil seeps from the housing located on the front of the engine block, dripping onto the exhaust and creating a burning oil smell. The leak worsens over time and can cause significant oil loss between changes. This issue is shared across many FCA vehicles using the 2.4L Tigershark engine.
records.solution: Replace the oil filter housing gasket and oil cooler O-rings (Mopar 68105583AF gasket kit). The repair requires removing the oil filter housing, cleaning the mating surfaces, and installing the new gaskets with proper torque. Some mechanics recommend replacing the entire housing assembly if the gasket surface is warped. Budget $250-$500 for parts and labor.
symptoms: Oil dripping on exhaust causing burning smell
Oil spots under the vehicle near the front of the engine
Visible oil seepage around oil filter housing
Smoke from engine bay at idle from oil on exhaust

records.title: Power Steering Rack Seal Leak (2nd Generation)
records.description: The power steering rack and pinion assembly on the 2nd generation Chrysler 200 (2015-2017) develops fluid leaks from the rack seals, particularly the inner tie rod seals. The leak is often hidden by the steering rack boots, so fluid loss goes unnoticed until the power steering pump begins whining from low fluid or steering effort increases. The 200 uses a hydraulic power steering system (not electric) which relies on adequate fluid levels.
records.solution: Inspect the steering rack boots by squeezing them — if they are full of fluid, the inner seals have failed. A steering rack seal kit is available but rack seal replacement is labor-intensive and often unsuccessful long-term. Most mechanics recommend replacing the entire steering rack assembly (remanufactured units from Cardone or Maval, $300-$500 for the rack). Budget $600-$1,200 for a complete rack replacement installed.
symptoms: Power steering fluid loss with no visible external leak
Power steering pump whining from low fluid
Fluid visible inside steering rack boots
Drips from steering rack area when boots tear open

records.title: Random Deployment of Active Head Restraints
records.description: The active (deployable) head restraints in the front seats can deploy randomly without any rear-end collision, sometimes striking the back of the occupant's head and causing minor injuries or concussions. The failure is attributed to a plastic component that breaks under stress or fatigue, triggering the spring-loaded restraint. Complaints span both generations of the 200.
records.solution: Replace the failed active head-restraint assembly in the affected seat with an updated unit; some owners report dealers reset/replace the mechanism. Check for any applicable TSB or goodwill coverage, as the part and labor otherwise come at owner expense.
symptoms: Head restraint suddenly deploys forward with no collision
Impact to the back of the head
Restraint stuck in the deployed position

citations.title: NHTSA PE19-014 Closing Report - Active Head Restraint Inadvertent Deployment
FCA Warranty Bulletin X84/X92 - Active Head Restraint Warranty Extension

records.title: Engine Stalling at Idle (Electronic Throttle Body)
records.description: The Chrysler 200 experiences intermittent engine stalling at idle, particularly when decelerating to a stop or sitting at traffic lights. The electronic throttle body accumulates carbon buildup that restricts airflow at idle, and the throttle position sensor can drift out of calibration. The 2.4L 4-cylinder is most commonly affected but the 3.6L V6 is also susceptible. The stall often occurs without a check engine light, making diagnosis frustrating.
records.solution: Clean the electronic throttle body with CRC throttle body cleaner — remove the air intake hose and spray the butterfly valve and bore while a helper opens the throttle plate. After cleaning, perform an idle relearn: key on (engine off) for 30 seconds, then start and let idle for 5 minutes without touching the gas pedal. If stalling persists, have the dealer reflash the PCM with the latest calibration and inspect the throttle body for TPS sensor failure. Replacement throttle body costs $200-$400.
symptoms: Engine stalls when coming to a stop
RPM drops very low then engine dies
Stalling without a check engine light

records.title: Transmission May Not Shift Into Park (Rollaway Risk) — 2015 V6
records.description: On 2015 200 V6 models built March-December 2014 with the 9-speed automatic, the parking pawl can become contaminated or the park rod can dislodge or break, so the transmission may fail to actually engage Park even though the dash shows 'Park.' The driver gets no warning, and the vehicle can roll away. This prompted NHTSA recall 15V-090, affecting roughly 22,000 U.S. vehicles.
records.solution: Under recall R08 / NHTSA 15V-090, dealers inspect the transmission and replace any unit with a contaminated pawl or broken/dislodged park rod free of charge. As a precaution, always set the parking brake. Verify completion by VIN at nhtsa.gov.
symptoms: Vehicle rolls away after shifting to Park
Dash shows Park but transmission not locked

citations.title: FCA Safety Recall R08 / NHTSA 15V-090 - Transaxle Park Rod

records.title: ZF 9-Speed Harsh/Rough Shifting, Lurching, and Hesitation
records.description: Beyond the recall-level neutral defect, owners broadly report poor driveability from the 9-speed automatic: hard or clunky shifts, lurching, hesitation off the line, slow first-gear engagement, and a tendency to hang in lower gears. The transmission was new and software-immature when introduced, and FCA issued multiple PCM/TCM reflashes to improve shift quality. Many owners still describe the shift behavior as rough even after updates.
records.solution: Dealers apply the latest PCM/TCM software calibrations to improve shift logic; on 2.4L cars the recall reprogram explicitly updates both modules to avoid undesirable shift quality. A transmission relearn/adaptation procedure and fresh ZF-spec fluid can help. Persistent cases may need valve body or mechatronic service.
symptoms: Slow/delayed first-gear engagement from a stop

records.title: ZF 9-Speed (9HP48) Transmission Unexpectedly Shifts to Neutral
records.description: Early second-generation 200 sedans with the ZF-sourced 9-speed automatic (948TE/9HP48) can unexpectedly drop into neutral while driving, causing a sudden loss of propulsion. The root cause is insufficient crimps on the terminals of the 26-way connector in the transmission range-sensor wire harness, which corrupts the transmission's gear-position signal. This triggered NHTSA recall 16V-529 covering the 2015 Chrysler 200 alongside related Jeep Cherokee, Renegade, RAM ProMaster City, and Fiat 500X models sharing the transmission.
records.solution: Under recall S55 / NHTSA 16V-529, dealers reprogram the Powertrain Control Module and Transmission Control Module and, if needed, replace the transaxle range-sensor wire harness free of charge. Owners should verify the recall has been completed via VIN at nhtsa.gov; out of warranty, harness/valve-body repairs typically run several hundred to over a thousand dollars.
symptoms: Transmission suddenly shifts to neutral while driving

citations.title: FCA Safety Recall S55 / NHTSA 16V-529 - 9-Speed Harness Crimp

records.title: ABS Module Internal Failure
records.description: ABS control module suffers internal failures due to short circuits in main circuit board. Prevents proper ABS operation and stores fault codes. While regular braking functions, vehicle loses anti-lock capability, traction control, and stability control.
records.solution: ABS module replacement or professional rebuild service. Check all wheel speed sensors and wiring before replacement. Many specialty shops offer rebuild for $300-500 with warranty. OEM module requires programming to VIN.
symptoms: No ABS function during hard braking

citations.title: Chrysler Safety Recall M10 / NHTSA 12V-197 - ABS/ESC Wiring

records.title: Alternator Failure (Multiple Recalls)
records.description: Both 3.6L and 5.7L engines with 160, 180, or 220 amp alternators prone to sudden failure. Voltage regulator in PCM can fail. Internal diode failures cause battery drain, fires, and loss of power while driving.
records.solution: Alternator replacement with updated unit per recall. Free replacement under recall for affected vehicles. Check PCM voltage regulator function. Verify alternator connections properly seated.
symptoms: Vehicle stalling or dying while driving

citations.title: FCA Safety Recall P60 / NHTSA 14V-634 - Alternator
FCA Safety Recall T36 / NHTSA 17V-435 - Alternator Diode Thermal Fatigue
FCA Safety Recall T75 / NHTSA 17V-741 - Alternator

records.title: Control Arm Bushing Premature Wear
records.description: OEM control arm bushings fail prematurely around 20,000-40,000 miles instead of typical 100,000+ lifespan. Bushings press-fitted into arms and cannot be replaced separately on most applications, requiring full control arm replacement.
records.solution: Replace lower/upper control arms as complete assemblies. Aftermarket polyurethane bushings (Prothane, Energy Suspension) offer longer life but harsher ride. Alignment required after replacement.
symptoms: Clunking or rattling over bumps at low speeds
Visible cracking or separation of bushing

records.title: Pentastar Cylinder Head Failure
records.description: Left cylinder head on early Pentastar engines suffers valve seat failure in cylinder #2. Valve seats overheat and drop out of aluminum head causing catastrophic misfires and potential engine damage. Design flaw later addressed.
records.solution: Complete cylinder head replacement required (left/driver's side). Cannot be repaired - must replace entire head with updated design. Some cases require both heads preventatively. Full coolant flush and thermostat replacement recommended.
symptoms: Check engine light with P0302 code
Rough idle and loss of power
Ticking or rattling from left side of engine

citations.title: FCA Bulletin 09-002-14 Rev. B - Left Cylinder Head Misfire Diagnosis and Replacement
FCA Warranty Bulletin D-14-12 / X56 - 3.6L Left Cylinder Head

records.title: Dashboard Warping and Deterioration
records.description: The dashboard pad on first-generation Chrysler 300 models warps and sinks, particularly near the driver's side defroster vent. The material deteriorates from UV exposure and heat cycling, becoming sticky or tacky in hot climates. Chrysler refused to address under warranty, stating it meets commercial standards.
records.solution: Install aftermarket dash cover (DashMat is most popular) or replace entire dashboard. Park in shade and use windshield sunshade to slow deterioration. No OEM recall or fix available.
symptoms: Visible gap between dashboard and windshield trim
Dashboard surface becoming sticky or tacky in hot climates

records.title: Rear Differential Whine and Bearing Failure
records.description: Rear differential develops whining from failed pinion bearing or ring/pinion wear. LX platform differentials have inherent whine, but excessive noise indicates bearing failure. Front differentials on AWD fail at 40,000-60,000 miles.
records.solution: Differential rebuild or replacement for severe cases. Drain differential fluid and inspect for metal shavings. Change fluid every 30,000-40,000 miles. Use proper limited-slip fluid if equipped. Pinion bearing replacement if caught early.
symptoms: Whining noise from rear during acceleration
Humming or roaring that increases with speed

records.title: EVAP System Small Leak (P0456)
records.description: Evaporative emission control system develops small leaks triggering P0456 code. Most commonly failed gas cap, chaffed EVAP purge pipe harness, or failed purge solenoid. Triggers check engine light and prevents emissions testing pass.
records.solution: Start with gas cap replacement ($20-40). If code returns, smoke test EVAP system to locate leak. Common fixes: replace purge solenoid, repair chaffed wiring harness, or replace cracked EVAP hoses.
symptoms: Check engine light with P0456 code
"Gas cap" warning even with cap tight

records.title: EVAP Leak Detection (NVLD/ESIM) Failure Triggers P0455/P0456 — Often Misdiagnosed as a Bad Gas Cap
records.description: The Chrysler 300 uses Chrysler's proprietary natural-vacuum leak detection hardware instead of a conventional pressure-based leak detection pump. On 2005-2006 cars this is the NVLD (Natural Vacuum Leak Detection) valve/solenoid; from 2007 onward it is the ESIM (Evaporative System Integrity Monitor), a small spring-and-diaphragm switch mounted on or next to the charcoal/vapor canister on the left underbody ahead of the fuel tank. Both work the same way: as the sealed EVAP system heats and cools, natural pressure/vacuum changes trip an internal switch the PCM reads to confirm the system is sealed. The diaphragm seal inside the NVLD/ESIM is a well-documented high-failure item — it stiffens, sticks, or loses its seal with age, so the PCM can no longer verify integrity and falsely reports a leak. The result is a check-engine light with P0456 (small leak, ~0.020 in.), P0455 (large leak), or P0457 (interpreted as loose/missing cap), even when the fuel system is actually sealed. Because the code wording points at the gas cap, this is very commonly misdiagnosed: owners and shops replace the cap (and often the purge valve and canister) repeatedly before discovering the NVLD/ESIM itself is the culprit. One 2012 300 SRT owner reported eight dealer visits — the ESIM and its seal replaced twice, plus a new filler neck, purge valve, and charcoal canister — before the leak code was resolved. The fault is an emissions/MIL issue only: it does not affect drivability or engine longevity, but it will fail an emissions/smog inspection and on some model years can disable remote start until cleared. A faint fuel-vapor smell is occasionally reported when an actual leak is present.
records.solution: Always start with the cheapest checks: tighten the fuel cap fully (listen for clicks), inspect the cap's O-ring seal, and replace a cracked/old cap with a genuine Mopar cap, then clear the code and drive several drive cycles. If the code returns, have a shop perform an EVAP smoke test — but note the small-leak verification monitor can fail even when a smoke test passes (some hairline EVAP-line cracks only open under vacuum, sealing under the positive pressure of a smoke machine). Inspect the EVAP lines and the purge valve/solenoid for cracks. If the cap, lines, and purge valve are good, replace the NVLD valve (2005-2006) or the ESIM (2007+); the ESIM is the common Mopar service part (e.g., P/N 4861959AD), typically about $40-$60 OEM ($20-$50 aftermarket), and unbolts from the canister with a few hand tools — a DIY-friendly job. On early cars where the NVLD/ESIM is integrated and sold only with the charcoal canister assembly, expect a higher parts cost. After replacement, clear the codes and complete the EVAP drive-cycle/monitor before re-testing for emissions. Total at a shop generally runs from roughly $150 (ESIM swap with labor) up to the $417-$476 range if a full vapor/charcoal canister assembly is needed.
symptoms: Check engine light / MIL on with no drivability change
Stored EVAP leak codes P0455, P0456, and/or P0457
Dashboard or message-center warning that the gas cap is loose/off even when it is tight
Repeat check-engine light after replacing the gas cap
Remote start disabled until the code is cleared (some model years)
Occasional faint fuel-vapor smell near the tank/filler when an actual leak is present

records.title: 5.7L HEMI Exhaust Manifold Bolt Failure
records.description: The 5.7L HEMI is notorious for exhaust manifold bolts breaking, especially on the passenger side. Thermal cycling causes bolts to become brittle and snap. Creates a ticking noise at cold startup that partially diminishes as engine warms but never fully goes away. Broken bolts can be extremely difficult to extract if snapped flush with the cylinder head.
records.solution: Extract broken bolts using ProMAXX drill template tool kit (PMXA200PROP) to safely extract without damaging cylinder head. Replace with upgraded Grade 8 double-ended studs and nuts instead of bolts. Apply anti-seize compound on new hardware. Consider Hooker Blackheart stainless replacement manifolds for a permanent upgrade on high-mileage vehicles.
symptoms: Ticking or exhaust leak noise at cold startup
Noise diminishes as engine warms but doesn't fully disappear
Visible exhaust soot around manifold flanges

records.title: Front Suspension Premature Wear (LX Platform)
records.description: First-generation Chrysler 300 models suffer from extremely rapid front suspension wear including tension struts (radius arms), inner and outer tie rods, lower control arm bushings, and sway bar end links. Bushings typically worn by 45,000-60,000 miles. This is a known endemic problem across all LX-platform vehicles (300, Charger, Magnum, Challenger).
records.solution: Replace tension struts, lower control arm bushings, tie rod ends, and sway bar end links as a complete set. Use quality aftermarket parts from Moog. Alignment required after repair. Inspect rear suspension cradle bushings simultaneously as they often wear at the same rate.
symptoms: Clunking or thumping noise from front end over bumps
Front end feels like it's collapsing over sharp bumps

records.title: Fuel Pump Relay Failure (TIPM-Related)
records.description: Fuel pump relay inside TIPM fails, preventing fuel pump activation. Vehicle has full electrical power but won't start due to no fuel delivery. Related to broader TIPM issue, specifically affects ASD/Fuel Pump relay circuits.
records.solution: TIPM replacement or professional rebuild focusing on fuel pump relay circuits. Temporary fix: tap on TIPM while starting (may restore connection). Long-term requires TIPM replacement ($700-1,200) or rebuild ($200-400).
symptoms: No-start condition with full electrical power
No fuel pump priming sound when key turned on
Vehicle starts sometimes, fails other times

records.title: HEMI 5.7L MDS Lifter and Camshaft Failure
records.description: The 5.7L HEMI V8 suffers from MDS lifter design defect where needle bearings are undersized. Lifters can be starved of oil during idle, causing seizure and catastrophic camshaft wear leading to engine failure.
records.solution: Replace all lifters, camshaft, and rocker arms as assembly. Use only OEM or high-quality lifters. Some owners disable MDS system. Use only SAE 5W-20 oil and maintain strict 3,000-5,000 mile oil change intervals.
symptoms: Persistent ticking or tapping noise from engine
Check engine light with misfire codes
Rough idle or loss of power

records.title: Pentastar 3.6L Oil Filter Housing Leak
records.description: The plastic oil filter housing develops cracks and gasket failures due to heat cycling. Chrysler discontinued original plastic part but never issued recall despite widespread problem.
records.solution: Replace with Dorman aluminum aftermarket housing (recommended by mechanics). OEM replacement is still plastic and will fail again. Complete coolant and oil system flush recommended.
symptoms: Oil leaking from front of engine near oil filter
Coolant leaking from oil filter housing area
Oil and coolant mixing in severe cases

records.title: Shifter Clip Failure - Vehicle Stuck in Park
records.description: A small plastic clip in the shifter mechanism breaks, causing the vehicle to become stuck in Park. Known design flaw in the first-generation LX platform vehicles. The clip is inexpensive but causes a completely disabled vehicle when it fails. Emergency brake override button near shifter can bypass the issue temporarily.
records.solution: Replace broken shifter clip (Mopar 4578446AA). Accessible by removing center console trim. Keep a spare clip in the glove box. Know the location of the brake override release near the shifter for emergency bypass.
symptoms: Vehicle stuck in Park, unable to shift
Shifter feels loose or has excessive play
Clicking sound when trying to shift out of Park

records.title: Monostable Shifter Rollaway Warning
records.description: Vehicles with monostable electronic gear selector may not adequately warn driver when door opened and vehicle not in PARK. Shifter returns to center after each shift, making gear selection unclear. Led to rollaway incidents subject to NHTSA recall.
records.solution: Dealer software update per NHTSA recall S27. Update improves warning chimes and messages when door opened out of Park. Always verify Park on dashboard display before exiting. Apply parking brake as backup.
symptoms: Vehicle rolls away after driver exits
Chime or warning may not sound when door opened in Drive
Vehicle not in Park despite shifter appearing neutral

citations.title: FCA Safety Recall S27 / NHTSA 16V-240 - Transmission Electronic Shift Lever

records.title: Starter Motor Failure
records.description: Starter motors fail prematurely or intermittently. Grinding noise during starting indicates worn starter gear. Electrical issues including corroded battery terminals, failed neutral safety switch, and bad starter relay contribute to no-start.
records.solution: Replace starter motor with updated unit. Before replacement, clean battery terminals and check battery voltage (12.4V+). Test neutral safety switch. Check starter relay and all wiring connections for corrosion.
symptoms: Grinding noise when trying to start
Clicking sound but engine doesn't crank
Intermittent starting - works sometimes, fails others

records.title: TIPM Electrical Failures
records.description: The TIPM main fuse and relay box circuit board traces blow from current spikes, shorts, or corrosion. Water intrusion common. Causes random electrical issues affecting fuel pump, lights, wipers, horn, windows, and safety systems.
records.solution: TIPM replacement or professional rebuild. Specialty companies offer rebuild services for $200-400 with warranty. OEM replacement from dealer $700-1,200 plus programming. Disconnect battery for 10 minutes to attempt temporary reset.
symptoms: Vehicle won't start but has power
Random activation of lights, wipers, or horn

records.title: Water Pump Failure and Cooling Leaks
records.description: Water pumps fail prematurely due to bearing and seal wear. Air pockets frequently form in cooling system after repairs. The 300 is difficult to properly bleed air from cooling system.
records.solution: Water pump replacement with new gaskets. Replace thermostat simultaneously per TSB. Complete coolant flush and proper bleeding essential. Use purge valve in front of upper intake manifold.
symptoms: Coolant leak from front of engine or below water pump
Whining or grinding noise from water pump

records.title: Window Regulator and Motor Failure
records.description: Power window regulators and motors fail frequently, particularly rear doors. Cable in regulator breaks or motor burns out. Window stuck in down or up position. Motor and regulator sold as assembly, cannot be separated.
records.solution: Replace window motor and regulator assembly. TSB #08-011-07 REV. A addresses front window issues requiring door module replacement. Check fuse first. Verify window switches functioning before replacing regulator.
symptoms: Grinding or clicking noise operating window
Window operates only in one direction

records.title: ZF 8-Speed Transmission Harsh Shifting
records.description: The ZF 8-speed automatic develops harsh shifting, especially in 2nd gear. Valve body is primary failure point. Cold shifting particularly problematic. Chrysler states "sealed for life" but failures occur before 150,000 miles.
records.solution: Dealer must replace transmission valve body under warranty if applicable. Ensure TCM updated to latest software. Perform Quicklearn procedure after work. Use only ZF-approved fluid.
symptoms: Harsh downshift from 2nd to 1st with jerking
Rough upshift from 2nd to 3rd with RPM spike
Noticeable clunk when shifting, especially cold

records.title: 3.5L V6 Engine Oil Sludge and Consumption
records.description: The 3.5L SOHC V6 in the 300M is susceptible to oil sludge formation, though less severely than the 2.7L. The high-performance tuning of the 3.5L in the 300M generates more heat than in other applications, and the oil drain-back passages in the heads can become restricted by sludge over time. Oil consumption of 1 quart per 1,000-2,000 miles is commonly reported. The issue is exacerbated by extended oil change intervals and conventional oil use. While not as catastrophic as the 2.7L, the sludge can lead to lifter noise, oil pressure loss, and eventually bearing damage if ignored.
records.solution: Start by verifying oil consumption and sludge severity: inspect under the oil fill cap/valve covers, check hot idle oil pressure with a mechanical gauge, listen for valvetrain noise, and perform a compression/leak-down test to rule out worn rings or valve seals. If sludge is moderate, remove the valve covers and oil pan to manually clean sludge, clear the cylinder head drain-back passages, replace the PCV valve, and refill with the correct viscosity full-synthetic oil plus a quality filter; if oil pressure is low, inspect/replace the oil pump pickup tube and screen, and repair bearing damage as needed. Engines with persistent consumption may also need valve stem seals or internal engine work, while severe sludge may justify replacing the engine rather than attempting repeated flushes, which can dislodge debris and worsen oil starvation. Typical costs range from about $300-$700 for inspection, cleaning, PCV service, and fresh oil, $800-$1,800 if oil pan/valve cover removal and pickup cleaning are required, and $2,500-$5,000+ for major internal repair or engine replacement.
symptoms: Lifter ticking noise on cold startup
Oil pressure gauge reading low at idle
Sludge visible on oil filler cap or valve cover
Blue smoke from exhaust on startup

records.title: Power Steering Pump Whine and Leak
records.description: The power steering pump develops a whining noise and leaks fluid from the shaft seal or reservoir. The whine is most noticeable at low speed turns and on cold mornings. Low fluid from leaks accelerates pump wear.
records.solution: Replace power steering pump and flush the system with fresh ATF+4 (Chrysler uses ATF as power steering fluid). Check all hoses and the rack and pinion for leaks. Use only Mopar-approved fluid.
symptoms: Fluid on driveway under front of car

records.title: Power Steering Rack Leak
records.description: The power steering rack on the 300M develops leaks from the rack seals, typically on the driver's side inner tie rod boot area. Power steering fluid leaks onto the subframe and can contaminate the front motor mount. The rack seal design is prone to failure due to heat exposure from the engine and exhaust proximity. Symptoms include low power steering fluid, groaning noise during turns, and stiff steering. The leak typically starts as a slow seep and progressively worsens. A full rack replacement is usually required as seal-only kits have poor success rates.
records.solution: Confirm the leak by cleaning the rack, filling the reservoir with the correct ATF+4 power steering fluid, and inspecting the driver-side inner tie rod boot, pressure/return line fittings, and pump area while the steering is turned lock-to-lock. If fluid is coming from inside the boot or rack end seals, replace the complete steering rack assembly rather than attempting a seal repair, then install new rack bushings/O-rings as needed, transfer or replace the outer tie rod ends if worn, refill and bleed the system, and perform a front-end alignment. Inspect the front motor mount and subframe bushings for fluid damage and replace any softened rubber components. Typical repair cost is about $700-$1,300 depending on rack brand, labor time, and whether tie rods, lines, or mounts are also replaced.
symptoms: Power steering fluid leak visible under vehicle
Groaning or whining noise during turns
Stiff steering, especially at low speeds
Wet or oily inner tie rod boots

records.title: 42LE Automatic Transmission Failure
records.description: The 42LE 4-speed automatic transmission in the 300M is prone to premature failure, including solenoid pack issues, torque converter clutch failure, and internal clutch pack wear. The high torque output of the 3.5L V6 stresses the transmission beyond its design limits. Harsh shifting, slipping, and limp mode are common symptoms. The transmission is shared with the Intrepid, Concorde, and LHS, and the failure patterns are identical across all platforms. The solenoid pack and connector are the most common failure points.
symptoms: Shudder during torque converter lockup at highway speed
Check engine light with transmission codes

records.title: Front Lower Control Arm Bushing Failure
records.description: The front lower control arm bushings wear out prematurely, causing clunking over bumps and imprecise steering. The Aspen shares its platform with the Dodge Durango and has the same front suspension weakness.
records.solution: Replace lower control arms with new bushings (complete arm replacement is easier than pressing new bushings). Moog RK620900 is a quality replacement. Alignment required after replacement.

records.title: 5.7L Hemi Exhaust Manifold Bolt Breakage
records.description: Exhaust manifold bolts break from thermal cycling, causing an exhaust leak that sounds like a ticking noise on cold start. The passenger side is most commonly affected. Ticking diminishes as the manifold expands when warm.
records.solution: Extract broken bolts and replace. If bolts break flush, drilling and easy-out extraction is required. Upgrade to stainless steel studs with copper locking nuts. Replace exhaust manifold gaskets during repair.

records.title: 5.7L HEMI MDS Lifter Tick and Camshaft Failure
records.description: Same HEMI 5.7L lifter/camshaft failure issue affecting all MDS-equipped engines. The MDS lifters have undersized needle bearings that fail from oil starvation at idle, causing catastrophic camshaft wear. Persistent ticking that worsens over time indicates lifter failure in progress.
records.solution: Replace all lifters, camshaft, and rocker arms. Consider Hellcat non-MDS lifter upgrade (8784AD) for MDS delete. Use Melling high-volume oil pump M10452HV (2009+). Maintain strict 3,000-5,000 mile oil change intervals with synthetic oil.
symptoms: Check engine light with misfire codes

records.title: Rear Differential Pinion Nut Loosening - Safety Recall
records.description: The rear axle pinion nut can loosen due to undersized pinion spline that allows relative motion between the nut and companion flange. If the nut loosens, the rear axle can lock up without warning, causing loss of vehicle control. Official recall issued for pinion nut retainer installation.
records.solution: Contact Chrysler dealer immediately for recall completion - free installation of pinion nut retainer. Have differential fluid checked and changed. Inspect pinion seal for leaks. TSB 18-006-10 REV. B addresses driveline clunking.
symptoms: Clunking sound when accelerating or decelerating
In worst case, sudden rear axle lockup

citations.title: Chrysler Safety Recall N08 / NHTSA 13V-038 - Rear Axle Pinion Nut

records.title: TIPM Electrical Module Failure
records.description: The Aspen shares the TIPM electrical module design with other Chrysler products. Fuel pump relay failure, random electrical activation, and battery drain are common. Same fundamental TIPM design flaw as Town & Country and 300.
records.solution: TIPM rebuild service (UpFix, Circuit Board Medics, MAKS TIPM) at $200-$400 is most cost-effective. New TIPM from dealer $800-$1,500 + programming. External fuel pump bypass cable available for fuel pump relay only.
symptoms: Fuel pump runs continuously with key off

records.title: Engine and Transmission Mount Deterioration
records.description: Engine mounts and the front (dogbone) mount break down, causing excessive engine movement and vibration. The transverse engine layout puts heavy stress on the mounts during acceleration and braking.
records.solution: Replace all three engine/transmission mounts as a set. The upper (torque strut/dogbone) mount typically fails first. Aftermarket mounts from Anchor or DEA are affordable alternatives to OE.

records.title: 2.5L V6 Head Gasket Failure
records.description: The Cirrus equipped with the Mitsubishi-sourced 2.5L V6 is prone to head gasket failure, often caused by overheating episodes. The engine's aluminum heads warp easily when overheated, making a simple gasket replacement insufficient without machining the heads.
records.solution: Replace the head gaskets and have both cylinder heads checked for warpage and machined flat if needed. Replace the thermostat and inspect the cooling system for the original overheat cause. The 2.4L four-cylinder is more reliable if available.
symptoms: Coolant loss with no visible leak

records.title: 41TE Automatic Transmission Solenoid Failure
records.description: The 41TE (A604) automatic transmission is prone to solenoid pack failure causing erratic shifting, limp mode, and harsh engagement. The 41TE was one of the first fully electronic automatic transmissions and reliability suffered.
records.solution: Replace solenoid pack assembly and fluid filter. Use only ATF+4 fluid. The updated solenoid pack from Mopar addresses the original design weaknesses. A full transmission rebuild may be needed if internal damage has occurred.

records.title: 2.7L V6 Engine Oil Sludge and Seizure
records.description: The 2nd generation Concorde (1998-2004) equipped with the 2.7L DOHC V6 suffers from the same catastrophic oil sludge issue as the Intrepid and Stratus. The engine's inadequate oil drain-back passages allow oil to cook and form sludge that clogs oil galleries, starves bearings of lubrication, and causes engine seizure. The internal water pump (driven by the timing chain) is an additional failure point that can introduce coolant into the oil and dramatically accelerate sludge formation. This is widely regarded as one of the worst engine designs in modern automotive history.
records.solution: Diagnosis starts with verifying low oil pressure using a mechanical gauge, inspecting under the oil filler cap/valve covers for sludge, checking for bearing noise, and testing for coolant contamination from the timing-chain-driven internal water pump. Mild cases may be addressed by removing the oil pan and valve covers, cleaning sludge from the pickup screen and oil return passages, replacing the oil pump, timing chain set, water pump, PCV valve, and performing multiple short-interval oil changes, but heavily sludged or knocking engines usually require complete engine replacement or professional rebuild. If coolant intrusion is present, the water pump and timing components must be replaced immediately, and any damaged bearings or seized rotating assembly make replacement the only practical repair. Typical costs range from about $1,500-$3,000 for partial cleanup and timing/water pump service to $4,000-$7,000+ for a quality rebuilt or replacement 2.7L engine installed.
symptoms: Oil pressure warning light flickering at idle
Heavy sludge visible on oil filler cap
Check engine light with misfire codes

records.title: 3.5L V6 Timing Belt Tensioner Failure
records.description: The 3.5L SOHC V6 (available across both Concorde generations) uses a timing belt with a hydraulic tensioner. The tensioner can fail, allowing the timing belt to skip teeth or break, resulting in catastrophic engine damage as the 3.5L is an interference engine. The tensioner's hydraulic damper loses its ability to maintain proper belt tension over time. Chrysler recommends timing belt replacement at 100,000 miles, but tensioner failures have been reported before this interval. The water pump is driven by the timing belt and should be replaced simultaneously.
symptoms: Rattling or slapping noise from front of engine
Check engine light with timing-related codes
Engine will not start (belt has broken or jumped)

records.title: Power Steering Hose and Rack Leak
records.description: The power steering high-pressure hose develops leaks at the crimped fittings, and the rack and pinion can leak from worn seals. Low fluid from leaks causes pump whine and eventual pump failure.
records.solution: Replace the leaking high-pressure hose and inspect the rack and pinion for seal leaks. If the rack is leaking, replacement is more cost-effective than rebuilding. Use ATF+4 as the power steering fluid (Chrysler spec).

records.title: 42LE Transmission Solenoid Pack Failure
records.description: The Concorde's 42LE 4-speed automatic transmission suffers from solenoid pack failures that cause erratic shifting, limp mode, and delayed engagement. The internal solenoid seals deteriorate, causing pressure loss and harsh or missed shifts.
records.solution: Replace the transmission solenoid pack assembly and filter. A full transmission fluid flush is recommended at the same time. If the transmission has been driven extensively in limp mode, internal hard parts may also be damaged.
symptoms: Transmission stuck in second gear (limp mode)
Check engine light with transmission codes
Delayed engagement when shifting to drive

records.title: A/C Compressor Failure and Interior Deterioration
records.description: A/C compressor failure is a known weak point. Interiors prone to rattles, worn trim, and failing seat motors. Headlights collect condensation inside the lens. Brake discs and pads wear quickly. These are known aging issues common to the Mercedes R170 platform.
records.solution: Replace A/C compressor. Source interior trim clips and parts from Mercedes SLK R170 donor vehicles. Headlight lenses can be resealed. Junkyard Mercedes SLK R170s are excellent parts sources since wheelbase and track width are identical to SLK320.
symptoms: Clicking or noise from A/C compressor
Interior rattles and trim pieces loosening

records.title: EGR Solenoid and Catalytic Converter Failure
records.description: The Crossfire (built on Mercedes SLK R170 platform, sharing 80% of components) commonly experiences EGR solenoid failures and premature catalytic converter failure. The EGR solenoid is the most common cause of check engine lights. Catalytic converter rattles and fails, especially noticeable when accelerating from cold.
records.solution: Replace EGR valve (Mercedes part A6121400060, fits Crossfire directly). Replace catalytic converter if rattling. Many Mercedes SLK R170 parts are direct replacements at lower cost. Use Mercedes dealer or independent Mercedes shop for best results.
symptoms: Rattling noise from underneath when accelerating from cold

records.title: Ignition Switch Failure - Key Sticking
records.description: The ignition switch (Mercedes-sourced) commonly fails, causing the key to stick and not turn. Prevents starting the vehicle. The switch mechanism wears internally. Higher failure rate than equivalent Mercedes models.
records.solution: Replace ignition switch assembly (Mercedes A2025450104). Use Mercedes OEM part for best quality. Graphite powder (not WD-40) can serve as temporary lubrication. Keep steering wheel centered when turning key to reduce stress on lock mechanism.
symptoms: Key gets stuck and can't be removed

records.title: Rear Coil Spring Breakage
records.description: Rear coil springs crack and break, especially in cold climates and on rough roads. The broken spring end can puncture a tire or damage the wheel well. The Crossfire uses Mercedes SLK components that are susceptible to corrosion.
records.solution: Replace both rear coil springs as a pair (even if only one has broken). Aftermarket springs from Eibach or Vogtland are available. Inspect for corrosion on remaining springs during routine maintenance.
symptoms: Rear of car sits lower on one side

records.title: SAM (Signal Acquisition Module) Water Intrusion
records.description: The SAM module (Mercedes-sourced body control module) located in the trunk area suffers from water intrusion causing corrosion of circuits. This triggers random electrical faults including lighting, power window, and central locking failures.
records.solution: Remove SAM module, clean circuit board of corrosion, and reseal the module housing. Identify and seal the water intrusion point (often the trunk gasket or rear window seal). Severe corrosion requires SAM replacement and coding.

records.title: A/C Compressor Clutch and Refrigerant Leak
records.description: The A/C compressor clutch wears out and the system develops refrigerant leaks at aging O-rings and hose connections. Many Fifth Avenues still have R-12 systems that require conversion to R-134a for continued use.
records.solution: Replace A/C compressor clutch or full compressor. Convert R-12 system to R-134a with conversion kit (includes adapter fittings, R-134a compatible oil, and new receiver drier). Replace all O-rings during conversion.

records.title: Front Ball Joint and Tie Rod End Wear
records.description: The front suspension ball joints and tie rod ends wear out from age, causing loose steering and clunking over bumps. The body-on-frame design with a heavy front end accelerates these wear items.
records.solution: Replace upper and lower ball joints and outer tie rod ends. Moog problem-solver parts are recommended for longer life. A front end alignment is required after any steering or suspension component replacement.

records.title: 3.3L/3.8L V6 Intake Manifold Plenum Gasket Oil Leak
records.description: The Chrysler 3.3L and 3.8L V6 engines (used in the Y-body Fifth Avenue/Imperial) develop a leak at the upper intake manifold plenum gasket. The plenum gasket degrades and allows oil from the PCV system to leak externally down the back of the engine and pool on top of the transaxle. The leak can be mistaken for a rear main seal leak due to its location. In severe cases, oil drips onto the exhaust manifold creating a burning oil smell and smoke.
records.solution: Replace the upper intake plenum gasket. This requires removing the upper intake manifold, which provides access to clean the EGR passages and throttle body at the same time. Use a Fel-Pro gasket rather than the OEM paper gasket. Clean the PCV valve and replace the PCV hose — excessive crankcase pressure from a stuck PCV valve accelerates the gasket leak.
symptoms: Oil leak on back of engine pooling on top of transaxle
Burning oil smell, especially at idle
Oil dripping from center/rear of engine
Light smoke from engine bay (oil on exhaust manifold)
Low oil level between oil changes

records.title: Power Seat Motor and Track Failure
records.description: The Fifth Avenue's 6-way power seat uses electric motors and a gear-driven track system that becomes noisy, slow, and eventually stops working. The seat track cables fray and jam in the guide tubes, and the electric motors burn out from increased resistance. The driver seat is most affected due to higher usage. The power lumbar support is also prone to failure — the inflatable bladder develops leaks and the pump motor fails.
records.solution: Lubricate the seat tracks and cable guides with white lithium grease — this can restore function to sluggish seats. If the motor has burned out, replacement motors are available from junkyard Fifth Avenue or New Yorker vehicles (same seat assembly). For the lumbar bladder, a manual lumbar support cushion is the practical alternative.
symptoms: Seat moves slowly or not at all when adjusting
Grinding or clicking noise from seat when operating
Electric motor hums but seat doesn't move (cable jam)

records.title: A604 (41TE) Transaxle Premature Failure
records.description: The Fifth Avenue uses the Chrysler A604 (41TE) fully electronic 4-speed transaxle, which was notorious for reliability issues in its early years. The solenoid pack and valve body suffer from design limitations that cause erratic shifting and limp mode. The transmission goes into "limp home" mode (locked in 2nd gear) as a protective measure when it detects solenoid or pressure errors. The Fifth Avenue's heavier curb weight compared to other A604-equipped vehicles accelerates wear.
records.solution: Replace the solenoid pack and valve body separator plate with updated parts. Change the ATF+4 fluid every 30,000 miles — the A604 is extremely sensitive to fluid condition. If the transmission has been running in limp mode repeatedly, internal clutch damage is likely and a rebuild is needed. A TransGo TFOD-3 reprogramming kit can be installed during a rebuild to improve shift quality.
symptoms: Limp mode — stuck in 2nd gear with check engine light
Harsh engagement from Park to Drive or Reverse
Delayed shifts with engine revving between gears

records.title: A604 (41TE) Ultradrive Limp Mode, Torque-Converter & Clutch Failure
records.description: Beyond the solenoid pack, the A604 (41TE) Ultradrive on V6/turbo LeBarons is infamous for dropping into limp mode — the transmission loses the higher gears and is stuck in second and reverse only, often after a speed/input sensor fault, voltage glitch, or internal clutch problem. Early Ultradrives also suffer clutch-pack and torque-converter wear (Chrysler made many running design changes early on), and use of the wrong fluid (Dexron/Mercon instead of ATF+4) quickly destroys them because the wrong fluid is too 'grabby.' Symptoms include harsh or no shifts, a buzzing/shuddering converter, and a transmission that won't upshift past second until restarted.
records.solution: Read transmission fault codes first — limp-in is frequently a sensor (input/output speed) or wiring/voltage issue that can be fixed without a teardown; clear the code after repair. Always service with the correct Mopar ATF+4 fluid and filter — never Dexron/Mercon. If clutch packs or the torque converter are worn (slipping, shudder, no 3rd/4th), the unit needs a rebuild with updated parts. Ensure charging-system voltage is stable, since low voltage triggers limp-in.
symptoms: Stuck in 2nd gear and reverse only (limp mode)
Transmission warning behavior that clears after restart

records.title: Auto Shutdown (ASD) Relay Failure — Cranks but Won't Start (No Spark/No Fuel)
records.description: The Auto Shutdown (ASD) relay powers the ignition coil, fuel injectors, and (via the fuel-pump relay) the fuel pump. When the ASD relay fails, contacts wear, or its connector corrodes, the engine cranks but gets no spark and no fuel and will not start; failure can also be intermittent, causing the car to die while driving and then restart later. On many LeBarons the relay sits on the driver's-side fender/strut tower. Because the same no-start symptom can come from the logic/power module or the pickup, the relay should be swapped or bench-tested to confirm.
records.solution: Test the ASD relay (listen for the brief click at key-on, verify it powers the coil/injector bus) and substitute a known-good relay; replace it if it fails to energize the coil/injector circuit. Clean and repair the relay connector and check for blown fuses and the PCM ground that controls the relay. Confirm fuel-pump and coil power return after replacement.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't start — no spark and no injector pulse
Intermittent stalling while driving, restarts after a wait
No buzz/prime from the fuel pump at key-on
No power to the ignition coil or injectors when cranking

records.title: Automatic Idle Speed (AIS) Motor Failure — Rough Idle, Stalling, Hunting
records.description: Chrysler's throttle-body and MPI fuel-injection LeBarons use an Automatic Idle Speed (AIS) motor (idle air control) that meters air around the closed throttle to keep the engine idling and to catch the idle when the A/C compressor cycles or when the throttle snaps shut. The AIS pintle and its passage carbon up, and the motor itself wears out, causing a rough or hunting idle, idle that surges up and down, stalling when coming to a stop or when the A/C kicks on, and sometimes a high idle that won't come down. The symptoms overlap with vacuum leaks, so the intake and vacuum lines must be checked first.
records.solution: Clean the AIS motor pintle and the air passage in the throttle body with throttle-body cleaner; if cleaning doesn't restore stable idle, replace the AIS motor. Confirm there are no intake/vacuum leaks (a common cause of the same symptoms) and that the throttle position sensor reads correctly before condemning the AIS. After replacement, let the system relearn idle.
symptoms: Rough or unstable idle, sometimes stalling at stops
Engine stalls when A/C compressor engages
High idle that won't return to normal
Stall when throttle is quickly released

records.title: A604 (41TE) Automatic Transaxle Electronic Shift Solenoid Failure
records.description: The LeBaron uses the Chrysler A604 (41TE) 4-speed electronically-controlled automatic transaxle. This was one of the first fully electronic automatics and its solenoid pack is the primary failure point. The solenoids develop internal leaks and electrical failures, causing erratic shifting, no-shift conditions, and limp mode (locked in 2nd gear). The transmission controller can also fail. The A604 was so problematic that Chrysler extended warranty coverage on early units.
records.solution: Replace the solenoid pack assembly (located in the valve body) with an updated unit. The solenoid pack is accessible by removing the side pan. A remanufactured solenoid pack from TransGo or Rostra is $150-250. If the transmission is in limp mode, scan for codes first — many limp mode events are caused by a speed sensor or input/output shaft sensor failure rather than the solenoid pack.
symptoms: Check engine light with P0700 and P07XX codes
Harsh or erratic shifting between all gears
Transmission bangs into gear from Park

records.title: Chronic Overheating — Wrong-Rotation Water Pump (1989+) & Cooling System Neglect
records.description: LeBaron overheating is common and one trap is unique to these cars: in 1989 the 2.2/2.5 switched to a counter-rotating (reverse-rotation) water pump driven off the back side of the timing/accessory belt, whereas 1980–1988 used a clockwise pump. Installing the wrong-rotation pump (or a generic replacement) pushes coolant the wrong way and the engine overheats even though the pump looks correct. Combined with the small radiators, electric-fan failures, and tired thermostats on these aging cars, owners report boiling coolant, rising temp gauge, and on turbo cars heat-soak that can crack a head or blow the gasket. Always match the pump to the engine's rotation.
records.solution: When replacing the water pump on a 1989+ engine, confirm it is the correct counter-rotating (reverse) pump for that year — do not fit an early clockwise pump. Then service the rest of the cooling system that commonly fails on these cars: thermostat, radiator (recore/replace if clogged), electric cooling-fan motor and fan relay/temp switch, hoses, and a proper coolant fill/bleed. On turbo cars, verify the fan operates to prevent post-shutdown heat-soak.
symptoms: Overheats after recent water-pump replacement (wrong-rotation pump)
Overheats at idle/in traffic but cools at speed

records.title: Convertible Top Hydraulic System and Fabric Deterioration
records.description: The LeBaron convertible's hydraulic top system suffers from cylinder leaks, pump failures, and the fabric top material degradating from UV exposure. The hydraulic cylinders develop internal seal leaks, causing the top to operate slowly or stop mid-cycle. The fabric top material shrinks and becomes brittle, developing tears at the stress points near the rear quarter windows. The rear plastic window yellows and becomes opaque, reducing rear visibility.
records.solution: Replace leaking hydraulic cylinders and top pump motor. Rebuild kits are available for the cylinders. For the fabric top, a complete convertible top replacement is available from Kee Auto Top or Robbins Auto Top. The rear window can be replaced separately with a new clear vinyl window. Apply 303 Fabric Guard to the top twice a year to extend fabric life.
symptoms: Top operates slowly or stops during operation
Hydraulic fluid leaking from cylinders behind rear seats
Top fabric torn or separating at seams
Top won't latch to windshield header

records.title: Coolant Temperature Sensor Failure — Hot Stall, Erratic Gauge, Hard Restart
records.description: The two-prong engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor at the thermostat housing feeds temperature data to the engine computer for fuel mixture and to the cooling-fan and gauge circuits. When it fails or its connector corrodes, the computer mis-fuels the engine: the car runs rough or floods when warm, stalls once hot, and is hard to restart until it cools (a classic heat-soak no/poor-start). The temperature gauge can read erratically or peg, and the electric cooling fan may not turn on, leading to overheating. Note this is the computer's ECT sensor, distinct from the dash gauge sending unit.
records.solution: Test the ECT sensor's resistance cold and hot against spec and inspect/repair the connector for corrosion; replace the sensor if out of range (Mopar coolant temperature sensor for the 2.2/2.5/3.0). Verify the cooling fan commands on and the gauge tracks after replacement. Rule out air in the cooling system and a stuck thermostat, which mimic an erratic gauge.
symptoms: Stalls or runs rough only after the engine is fully warm
Hard to restart when hot, fine again after cooling
Cooling fan doesn't come on / intermittent overheating
Poor fuel economy and black smoke (over-rich when cold-signal stuck)

records.title: Distributor Hall-Effect Pickup Heat-Soak Failure — Intermittent No-Spark Stall
records.description: The distributor pickup is a three-wire Hall-effect sensor that tells the engine computer the engine is turning so it can fire spark and injectors. These pickups are prone to heat-related, intermittent failure: the car runs fine cold but suddenly stalls once the engine bay heats up, then restarts after it cools (heat-soak). The Hall sensor can fail without setting a code, and because the computer sees no engine-rotation signal, it cuts fuel and spark entirely. On the 3.0L, an intermittent no-spark can also come from the coil or ignition module, so the pickup must be confirmed with a scope/voltage test.
records.solution: Verify the pickup's 8V supply, ground, and switching 0–5V signal while cranking (a scope best catches heat-related dropout). Replace the distributor pickup/Hall sensor (or the distributor assembly) if the signal drops out when hot. Inspect the wiring and connector for heat damage. On the 3.0L also test the coil and ignition control module before condemning the pickup.
symptoms: Engine stalls suddenly after warming up
Restarts only after sitting and cooling down
Crank-no-start with no spark when hot
Intermittent stalling that worsens in hot weather
No fault code stored despite the stall

records.title: Engine Controller Failure (Logic/Power Module, SMEC, SBEC) — No-Start / Stalling
records.description: Early LeBarons use a two-box system (separate logic module in the kick panel and power module near the battery); 1988+ cars use the combined SMEC, and later cars the SBEC. The power-module/driver section is a known weak point: heat and vibration crack solder joints and fail the injector/ignition drivers, producing intermittent stalling, no-spark/no-fuel no-starts, or a car that runs poorly and drops into limp-in. Fault codes (read by cycling the key on-off-on) help point at it, but the module can fail without a clean code. The logic module also enters limp-in and reduces performance when it loses key sensor data.
records.solution: Pull stored fault codes via the key-on/off flash-code method to confirm a controller or driver fault, then replace the failed module (logic module, power module, SMEC, or SBEC) with a known-good or remanufactured unit and ensure clean grounds and battery voltage. Repair corroded connectors. Verify charging-system voltage, since the power module also regulates the alternator field and is stressed by a bad alternator/battery.
symptoms: Intermittent stalling, sometimes restarts after cooling
Crank-no-start with no spark or no injector pulse
Erratic or no charging voltage (early power module)
Fault codes pointing to driver circuits or no-start

records.title: Fuel Injector Clogging and Leaking
records.description: Fuel injectors develop clogs and O-ring leaks from age and fuel deposit buildup. Clogged injectors cause misfires and poor fuel economy. Leaking injector O-rings create a fire hazard from fuel dripping onto the hot engine.
records.solution: Clean or replace fuel injectors. Professional ultrasonic cleaning restores most clogged injectors. Replace all injector O-rings with Viton (fuel-resistant) O-rings. Use fuel injector cleaner additive periodically as preventive maintenance.

records.title: 2.5L and 3.0L Head Gasket Failure
records.description: The LeBaron's 2.5L 4-cylinder and 3.0L Mitsubishi V6 engines both suffer from head gasket failure. The 2.5L uses a composite head gasket that deteriorates, allowing coolant into the combustion chambers and oil passages. The 3.0L Mitsubishi V6 develops gasket failure between cylinders, causing compression loss. Both engines overheat easily due to the LeBaron's limited airflow in the engine bay, particularly the convertible model where underhood temperatures run higher.
records.solution: Replace head gaskets with Fel-Pro MLS (multi-layer steel) gaskets rather than composite replacements. Have heads checked for warpage and resurfaced. Replace the thermostat and flush the cooling system. On the 2.5L, inspect the head for cracks around the exhaust valve seats — a common failure point that requires a replacement head.
symptoms: Coolant loss with no external visible leak

records.title: HVAC Blower Motor Resistor Failure — Fan Works Only on High
records.description: The heater/AC blower resistor block that controls the lower fan speeds is a common failure on these cars. When it burns out, the low and medium fan settings stop working and the blower runs only on High (which bypasses the resistor). The resistor typically overheats and fails because an aging, current-hungry blower motor draws too much current through it, so a resistor that's replaced alone often fails again if the worn motor isn't addressed. On the LeBaron the blower/resistor is buried under the dash/behind the glovebox, making access tight.
records.solution: Replace the blower motor resistor; because resistor failure is usually driven by a worn high-draw blower motor, inspect the motor and replace it at the same time if it's noisy or drawing high current. Check the blower connector for heat damage/melting and repair as needed. Confirm all fan speeds work after the repair.
symptoms: Blower only works on the High setting
No airflow on some settings, normal on others

records.title: Instrument Cluster / Speedometer & Odometer Failure
records.description: LeBaron instrument clusters (both standard and the digital dash) are a common failure point. The speedometer reads zero or erratically and the odometer stops counting, usually from a failed vehicle speed sensor (VSS) on the transaxle, a stripped odometer drive gear / worn speedometer cable on cable-driven clusters, or internal cluster/solder failures. On the digital dash, segments drop out or the speedometer sticks at 0. Because a dead VSS also feeds the computer, it can additionally affect shift quality and idle, not just the gauge.
records.solution: Diagnose whether the fault is the VSS (test/replace the speed sensor on the transaxle), the speedometer cable / odometer drive gear (replace worn gear or cable on cable clusters), or the cluster itself. Failed clusters can be rebuilt by a cluster-repair specialist (re-soldering, replacing the stepper/odometer gears) rather than buying a scarce used unit. Check the cluster/instrument fuse and connector first.
symptoms: Digital dash segments missing or flickering
Dash gauges dead while other electrics work
Erratic shifting tied to a failed speed sensor

records.title: Mitsubishi 3.0L V6 Valve Stem Seal / Valve Guide Wear — Oil Consumption and Blue Smoke on Startup
records.description: The Mitsubishi-sourced 3.0L V6 is well known for oil consumption caused by hardening valve stem seals and, at higher mileage, worn valve guides. As the seals shrink/harden, oil seeps past the valve stems while the car sits, then burns off on startup as a puff of blue-gray smoke that clears within 10-30 seconds. This is distinct from head-gasket failure (which burns coolant): compression is typically normal and the car steadily consumes oil between changes. Replacing seals alone often fails within 10-20k miles because worn guides provide the slop that destroys the new seals; a plugged PCV drain in the valve covers can worsen consumption. The 2.2L/2.5L fours can also develop valve-seal seep-down smoke with age, but the 3.0L V6 is the standout.
records.solution: Confirm the diagnosis first (normal compression with blue smoke points to seals/guides, not rings). Replace the valve stem seals with high-quality positive-type seals; many can be done with the head on using compressed air to hold the valves. If smoke persists and plugs foul, the guides are worn and the head must come off for guide replacement/machining. Check the PCV system and valve-cover drain holes for blockage.
symptoms: Smoke after idling that clears when driving

records.title: Power Window Motor Failure
records.description: Power window motors fail from worn brushes and aged wiring. The driver side window sees the most use and fails first. Corroded connectors in the door jamb harness can also cause intermittent window operation.
records.solution: Replace window motor. Check the wiring harness in the door jamb for broken wires where it flexes. Clean or replace corroded connectors. The master window switch should also be tested as a potential cause.
symptoms: Motor clicks but window does not move

fixParts.note: Cardone 42-406. Fitment confirmed against the ShowMeTheParts catalog for this vehicle's year and engine.
