records.title: Timing Belt Wear and Breakage (2.2L/2.5L/3.0L) — Stranding No-Start
records.description: All LeBaron engines are belt-driven overhead-cam designs with a rubber timing belt that has a finite service life (roughly 60,000 miles). The Chrysler 2.2L/2.5L four-cylinder engines are non-interference designs, so a snapped or skipped belt leaves the car stranded but does not bend valves. The belts age, harden, and can skip a tooth or shred, causing a sudden stall/no-start or rough running. The Mitsubishi-sourced 3.0L V6 is an interference engine and far less forgiving — belt neglect there risks valve-to-piston contact and bent valves. Because these cars are now decades old, many run on original or badly overdue belts, making this a leading cause of roadside breakdowns.
records.solution: Replace the timing belt on schedule (about every 60,000 miles), and replace the water pump, tensioner, and idler pulleys at the same time since they sit behind the belt. Verify correct belt tension and that all cam/intermediate/crank timing marks align. If the belt has already skipped, re-time the engine; on the interference 3.0L V6, inspect for bent valves before returning to service.
symptoms: Sudden engine stall with no restart
Sluggish acceleration / poor performance after belt skip
Rattling or slapping noise from front of engine
Rough running after the belt jumps a tooth

records.title: Turbocharger Bearing/Seal Failure (Oil Starvation, Blue Smoke)
records.description: The turbocharged LeBarons (Garrett T3-based Turbo I and the higher-boost Turbo II) suffer turbo center-bearing and oil-seal wear from oil starvation at cold start and shutdown, and from coking when the engine is shut off hot without a cool-down. Worn seals let engine oil pass into the intake or exhaust, causing blue smoke (especially on startup or boost), oil consumption, and eventually a frozen or noisy turbo. The small-frame T3 is prone to burnt oil cutting a groove in the turbine shaft so the seals can no longer hold oil. Lack of oil changes and hard acceleration on a cold engine accelerate the failure.
records.solution: Replace or rebuild the turbocharger (CHRA/cartridge) with new bearings and seals; on the T3, install a wear sleeve if the shaft is grooved. Address the root causes: change oil on a strict interval with a quality oil, allow the engine to idle ~30–60 seconds before shutdown after hard driving, and avoid full boost until oil is warm. Inspect and clean the turbo oil feed/drain lines, which can clog with coked oil and starve the bearing.
symptoms: Blue/gray smoke from the exhaust, worst on startup or under boost
Excessive oil consumption with no external leak
Whining, whistling, or grinding noise from the turbo
Oil film inside the intake hose or intercooler piping

records.title: 3.5L V6 Excessive Oil Consumption
records.description: The 3.5L SOHC V6 in the LHS develops excessive oil consumption over time, typically burning 1 quart every 1,000-2,000 miles. The primary causes are worn valve stem seals that allow oil to leak past the valve guides into the combustion chamber, and piston ring wear. Oil sludge formation in the head drain-back passages contributes to the problem by restricting oil return flow. Blue smoke on startup is the hallmark symptom. The issue is progressive and worsens with mileage. Extended oil change intervals and conventional oil accelerate the problem.
records.solution: Confirm the source of oil consumption by checking for blue smoke after an overnight sit, inspecting spark plugs for oil fouling, performing a compression and leak-down test, and removing the valve covers to inspect for sludge and restricted drain-back passages. If compression is good, replace the valve stem seals on both cylinder heads, clean the head drain-back areas and valve covers, install fresh spark plugs, and switch to a high-detergent synthetic oil with shorter 3,000-5,000 mile service intervals; this repair typically runs about $800-$1,800 depending on labor. If leak-down or compression testing shows worn piston rings or cylinder wear, the permanent fix is an engine overhaul or replacement short block/used engine, which commonly costs $2,500-$5,000+. Continue monitoring oil level closely between services to prevent low-oil damage and hot idle oil pressure problems.
symptoms: Blue smoke from exhaust on cold startup
Oil consumption of 1 quart per 1,000-2,000 miles
Low oil pressure at idle when hot
Sludge buildup on valve covers and oil cap

records.title: 3.5L V6 Intake Manifold Runner Control Failure
records.description: The 3.5L V6 intake manifold runner control (IMRC) valve actuator fails, causing a loss of low-end torque and a check engine light. The IMRC system varies intake runner length for optimal power across the RPM range.
records.solution: Replace the intake manifold runner control actuator. Some aftermarket solutions include deleting the system and pinning the runners in the open position, though this reduces low-end torque slightly.

records.title: Power Steering Pressure Hose and Rack Seal Leaks
records.description: The LHS power steering system develops leaks at the high-pressure hose crimp fittings and the steering rack input shaft seal. Low fluid causes the pump to whine and can lead to sudden loss of power assist while driving.
records.solution: Replace the high-pressure power steering hose and inspect the rack seals. If the rack is leaking, a rebuilt rack is more cost-effective than seal replacement. Flush the power steering system with fresh ATF+4 fluid.

records.title: 42LE Automatic Transmission Failure
records.description: The 42LE 4-speed automatic transmission in the LHS shares the same failure patterns as the Intrepid, Concorde, and 300M. Solenoid pack failures, torque converter clutch issues, and internal clutch pack wear lead to harsh shifting, slipping, and limp mode. The LHS's heavy curb weight and 3.5L V6 torque output stress the transmission. The solenoid pack and transmission connector are the most common failure points and can be serviced without removing the transmission.
symptoms: Stuck in limp mode (2nd gear only)
Shudder at highway speed during TCC lockup
Check engine light with P0700 series codes

records.title: 41TE/42LE Transmission Solenoid and Shift Issues
records.description: The automatic transmission develops solenoid pack failures and valve body wear causing harsh shifts, delayed engagement, and limp mode. The transmission control module can also develop cold solder joints causing intermittent issues.
records.solution: Replace solenoid pack and filter. Inspect the valve body for wear. If the TCM is suspected, check connections and re-solder cold joints if possible. Use only Mopar ATF+4 fluid.

records.title: Electronic Air Suspension Compressor Failure
records.description: The rear electronic air suspension compressor fails, causing the rear of the vehicle to sag. The air springs can also develop leaks where the rubber meets the upper mount. Replacement compressors are expensive and hard to find.
records.solution: Replace the air suspension compressor or convert to conventional coil springs using a conversion kit (Arnott C-2227). The coil spring conversion eliminates the maintenance-prone air system entirely and is the most popular long-term fix.

records.title: 3.3L/3.8L V6 Engine Oil Leaks
records.description: The 3.3L and 3.8L pushrod V6 engines in the New Yorker develop multiple oil leaks with age, particularly from the valve cover gaskets, rear main seal, oil pan gasket, and timing cover seal. The rubber gaskets and seals harden and shrink from heat cycling over time. While these engines are otherwise quite reliable and long-lasting, the oil leaks can cause exhaust smoke, oil dripping on the driveway, and low oil level if not monitored. The rear main seal is the most expensive repair due to labor access requirements.
records.solution: Diagnose the leak by thoroughly cleaning the engine, adding UV dye to the oil if needed, and inspecting common leak points on the 3.3L/3.8L V6 including the valve cover gaskets, oil pan gasket, timing cover/front crank seal, and rear main seal. Repair involves replacing the failed gasket or seal, checking the PCV/breather system so crankcase pressure is not forcing oil past seals, and resealing mating surfaces with the correct RTV where specified by Chrysler. Valve cover and oil pan gasket repairs are usually the least expensive, while timing cover and especially rear main seal repairs require much more labor because of front accessory or transmission removal. Typical costs range from about $150-$400 for valve cover or minor upper-engine leaks, $300-$700 for oil pan or timing cover resealing, and roughly $700-$1,400 for a rear main seal depending on labor rates.
symptoms: Oil spots on driveway or garage floor
Burning oil smell from engine bay
Visible oil on engine exterior and exhaust manifold
Smoke from engine bay after extended driving

records.title: Power Window Motor and Regulator Failure
records.description: Power window motors and regulators fail frequently, especially on the driver's side which sees the most use. The motor gears strip and the regulator cables can fray, leaving the window stuck down or inoperable.
records.solution: Replace window motor and regulator as a complete assembly. Driver's side typically fails first. Check the master window switch on the driver's door as switch failures can mimic motor problems.
symptoms: Window won't go up or down

records.title: A604 Ultradrive Transmission Premature Failure
records.description: The New Yorker's A604 (41TE) 4-speed automatic was one of the first electronically controlled transmissions and is notorious for premature failure. The solenoid pack, input/output speed sensors, and clutch packs wear out, causing erratic shifting and complete failure.
records.solution: Replace the solenoid pack and speed sensors for early symptoms. Once slipping occurs, a full rebuild or remanufactured transmission is required. Use only ATF+4 fluid — other fluids accelerate clutch wear.
symptoms: Stuck in second gear limp mode
Delayed engagement into drive or reverse

records.title: A/C Compressor Failure and Rear A/C Performance Loss
records.description: The A/C compressor fails prematurely, often between 60,000-100,000 miles, leaving the entire cabin without cooling. Additionally, the rear A/C system (standard on most trims) can lose effectiveness even when the compressor is functional due to a clogged rear A/C expansion valve or low refrigerant charge. Given the Pacifica is a family minivan, A/C failure creates a significant usability issue, especially in summer with children.
records.solution: For compressor failure, replace the A/C compressor, receiver/drier, and expansion valve as a system. Flush the condenser to remove debris from the failed compressor. For rear A/C only issues, check the rear expansion valve (often clogged) and ensure the system is fully charged with the correct amount of R-1234yf refrigerant. A full compressor replacement runs $1,000-$1,800.
symptoms: A/C blows warm air from all vents
Rear A/C colder or warmer than front (inconsistent)
Grinding or rattling noise from compressor area
A/C works intermittently then fails completely

records.title: 3.6L Pentastar Engine Stalling and Head Gasket Failure
records.description: The 3.6L Pentastar V6 in Pacifica models suffers from engine stalling due to loose ground connections (recall NHTSA 19V348), crankshaft position sensor sync issues, and premature head gasket failures typically around 75,000-85,000 miles. Cooling system failures can lead to coolant entering the combustion chamber, requiring complete engine replacement.
records.solution: Check recall NHTSA 19V348 for ground connection fix. For head gasket, use Felpro head gasket set HS26517PT. Monitor coolant level frequently - dropping level with no visible leak is a red flag. If coolant enters oil system, engine replacement may be required ($5,000-$8,000). 2020+ models reportedly have improved head gasket design.
symptoms: Engine stalls without warning while driving
Loss of power steering assist during stall
Coolant level dropping without visible external leak

citations.title: FCA Recall U01 / NHTSA 18V-049 - Engine Stall Due to Software Issue

records.title: Transmission Harsh 3-4 Shift and Shudder (9-Speed)
records.description: The ZF 9HP 9-speed automatic transmission in the Pacifica exhibits harsh or jerky 3-4 shifts, shuddering during light throttle acceleration at 25-40 mph, and occasional hesitation when downshifting. The 9-speed has had multiple software calibration updates since launch, and the adaptive learning can become confused by varied driving patterns. Cold weather worsens the harsh shifting. The issue persists across multiple model years despite ongoing TSBs.
records.solution: Visit a dealer for the latest transmission control module (TCM) software update — Stellantis has released numerous calibration updates (most recent as of 2025 is TSB 21-013-24 or newer). After the update, the transmission needs a re-adaptation period of 500-1,000 miles of mixed driving. If harsh shifting persists, a transmission fluid drain and refill with Mopar ZF 9-speed fluid may help. In severe cases, valve body replacement resolves persistent harsh shifts ($1,000-$2,000).
symptoms: Shudder during light acceleration at 25-40 mph
Hesitation or hunting between gears on hills

records.title: Plug-In Hybrid Battery Fire Risk (PHEV)
records.description: The high-voltage battery pack in Pacifica PHEV models can develop internal short circuits and spontaneously catch fire, even while parked and turned off. Stellantis recalled 24,000+ vehicles after 7+ fire incidents. A previous software fix was deemed not effective and a second recall was issued. Recall 72B / NHTSA 24V-482 provides free battery replacement.
records.solution: Park vehicle outside immediately, away from structures, until recall is completed. Do NOT charge the vehicle until recall remedy is applied. Contact Chrysler at 800-853-1403 for recall status. Recall 72B provides free diagnostic software update and battery replacement if abnormality detected.
symptoms: Service Hybrid Electric Vehicle System warning
In worst case, fire while parked

citations.title: FCA Recall 73B / NHTSA 24V-536 - 2017-2018 Pacifica PHEV High-Voltage Battery
FCA Recall 72B / NHTSA 24V-538 - 2019-2021 Pacifica PHEV High-Voltage Battery
FCA Recall 52D / NHTSA 26V-362 - 2020-2022 Pacifica PHEV Battery Fire Risk

records.title: Hybrid Transmission Wiring Harness Short (PHEV)
records.description: Internal transmission wiring connectors in PHEV models can short circuit, causing unexpected engine shutdown while driving. The low-voltage wiring harness within the transmission develops shorts, causing the gas engine to shut down and the vehicle to go into limp mode or lose motive power entirely. Recall 03A / NHTSA 23V010 issued.
records.solution: Contact dealer for Recall 03A / NHTSA 23V010 inspection. Dealers will inspect and if necessary replace the entire transmission. Keep gas tank above quarter-full so gas engine can take over if electric system fails.
symptoms: Engine suddenly shuts off while driving

citations.title: FCA Recall 03A / NHTSA 23V-010 - Loss of Motive Power

records.title: Power Liftgate Malfunction and Failure to Open/Close
records.description: The power liftgate struts, latch assembly, and control module fail, causing the liftgate to not open or close fully, reverse direction mid-travel, or stop responding to button presses entirely. The hydraulic struts lose pressure and cannot hold the liftgate open, letting it fall. The latch assembly sensor can also malfunction, causing the system to think the liftgate is not fully latched and triggering warning chimes. Minivan owners with frequent cargo access are most affected.
records.solution: Start by checking the liftgate latch striker alignment — misalignment causes latch sensor errors. Replace the power liftgate struts if the gate will not stay open or opens slowly (Mopar 68385386AA or Stabilus equivalents, $50-$100 each). If the liftgate motor or control module has failed, the entire power liftgate motor assembly needs replacement ($300-$700). Reset the liftgate control module by disconnecting the battery for 10 minutes.
symptoms: Liftgate does not open or close with button press
Liftgate will not stay open — falls slowly or quickly
Warning chime indicating liftgate not latched
Liftgate opens only partway then stops

records.title: Power Sliding Door Actuator and Motor Failure
records.description: Power sliding door lock actuators and drive motors fail, causing doors to not open or close automatically, get stuck partially open, or make grinding/clicking noises. Most common non-powertrain complaint among Pacifica owners. The actuator's internal mechanism sticks in the lock position.
records.solution: Replace sliding door lock actuator and/or drive motor. Remove interior door trim panel to access. Right (passenger) actuator Mopar 68185976AD, left (driver) actuator 68185977AD, motor 68303288AC. Can be DIY in 1-2 hours. Lubricate door track rails with white lithium grease regularly as preventive maintenance.
symptoms: Sliding door won't open or close automatically
Whirring, grinding, or clicking noise from door
Sliding Door Open warning despite door being closed

records.title: TPMS Sensor Battery Failure and False Warnings
records.description: The tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) sensors experience premature battery failure, causing persistent TPMS warning lights and inaccurate pressure readings. The factory TPMS sensors use lithium batteries with a typical lifespan of 5-7 years, but many Pacifica owners report failures as early as 3-4 years. When one sensor battery dies, the system displays a general TPMS warning, and the driver cannot determine which tire actually needs attention without a TPMS scan tool.
records.solution: Replace the failed TPMS sensor(s). TPMS sensors cannot be battery-replaced — the entire sensor unit must be swapped. OEM sensors (Mopar 68399563AA) cost $40-$60 each and must be programmed to the vehicle using a TPMS relearn tool or dealer scan tool. Aftermarket programmable sensors from Autel or ATEQ are available for less ($20-$35 each). Replace all four sensors simultaneously if the vehicle is 5+ years old to avoid return visits.
symptoms: TPMS warning light stays on despite correct tire pressures
Dash shows dashes instead of pressure readings for one or more tires
Intermittent TPMS warning that comes and goes
TPMS light comes on in cold weather and stays on
All tire pressures show as 0 psi on the display

records.title: UConnect Infotainment System Freezing and Rebooting
records.description: The 8.4-inch UConnect 4 and 10.1-inch UConnect 5 infotainment systems freeze, go blank, or reboot randomly. Affects radio, touchscreen, GPS, rearview camera, Bluetooth, and rear entertainment. A class-action lawsuit covers 8.4A and 8.4AN systems. Some owners have had screens replaced multiple times without lasting resolution.
records.solution: Try soft reset by holding volume and tuner knobs for 10-20 seconds. For UConnect 4C (2018+), pull radio fuse F76 for hard reset. Request latest software update from dealer before screen replacement. Screen replacement for delamination issues.
symptoms: Screen goes blank or reboots while driving
Radio changes stations or volume on its own
records.contentUpdateSummary: Removed unrelated parts; clarified software-first repair.

records.title: 3.5L Cam/Crank Sensor O-ring & Valve Cover Oil Weeping
records.description: The Chrysler 3.5L SOHC V6 is known to weep oil from the camshaft position sensor O-ring and valve-cover sealing surfaces as the rubber hardens with age. On the low-mileage, long-parked Prowler fleet this shows up as oil residue on the block, a burning-oil smell, and occasionally an oil-contaminated cam sensor connector. Left unaddressed it can foul the sensor and contaminate wiring.
records.solution: Clean and pinpoint the source (cam sensor O-ring vs valve cover gasket vs cam bearing cap). Replace the hardened cam position sensor O-ring and/or valve cover gaskets with updated seals; clean the sensor connector so oil cannot re-wick into it. Address the leak before it contaminates the cam sensor or ignition components.
symptoms: Oil in the cam sensor connector
Low oil level over time on a garaged car

records.title: 42LE Shift Solenoid Pack Failure / Limp-In Mode
records.description: The rear-mounted 42LE (A606) automatic can drop into limp-in (fail-safe) mode when the electronic shift solenoid pack develops internal faults. Symptoms are the transmission locking into a single gear (commonly 2nd, or only 1st and reverse) until the ignition is cycled, often accompanied by a check-engine/transmission light. This is distinct from the fluid-overheating and AutoStick harsh-shift issues: here the solenoid pack itself (or its wiring/connector) is the root cause and typically sets solenoid-performance codes.
records.solution: Scan for codes and confirm with pressure/solenoid tests before parts replacement. Replace the shift solenoid pack (reman Mopar A606/42LE solenoid pack, PN 4539766) along with a fresh filter and correct ATF; cycling the ignition off/on temporarily clears limp mode as a get-home measure. Verify the transmission connector and internal wiring harness are not the fault before condemning the pack.
symptoms: Transmission stuck in one gear (limp mode)
Only 1st and reverse available after warm-up
Harsh or no upshift with warning light

records.title: Cable-Type Power Window Regulator Failure (Obsolete OEM Part)
records.description: The Prowler uses a cable-driven window regulator whose plastic cable-guide tubing and jacket are subjected to severe repeated bending stress. Over time the cable jacket cracks and the plastic guides break, so the window binds, drops, will not seal against the convertible top, or makes a faint ratcheting noise instead of moving smoothly. Because window position must match the convertible-top seal, a failed regulator also causes wind/water leaks. The OEM regulators are largely obsolete/discontinued, making this a high-demand pain point for owners.
records.solution: Because new OEM regulators are obsolete, owners rely on rebuild/reinforcement services that replace the failure-prone plastic tubing with stainless-steel braiding and add a metal-plated glass carrier. After repair, set the window height with the adjustment screws so the glass evenly compresses the top seals per the owner's manual. Budget per-door.
symptoms: Window will not go all the way up with top up
Window drops or binds in the track
Faint ratcheting noise from the door
Window heights differ top-up vs top-down
Wind/water leak at the top seal

records.title: Convertible Top Rear Window Separation & Top Leaks
records.description: The Prowler's hand-built folding soft top is prone to the flexible rear window delaminating/separating from the surrounding top fabric as the bonding adhesive ages and dries out, typically starting at the lower corners. Owners also report the top scuffing the area just below the rear glass when the multi-stage folding sequence in the owner's manual isn't followed exactly, and water leaks past aged rubber seals. Because the top is a low-volume, hand-assembled design, replacement tops are expensive and hard to source.
records.solution: Minor separations are re-bonded with vinyl/window adhesive (DIY or upholstery shop). Owners are advised to inspect all seals for dry-rot and adjust the frameless door glass so it compresses evenly against the top seals to stop leaks. Severe tears, delamination, or scuffing require a full replacement top from a specialty Prowler supplier, and owners must follow the manual's open/close procedure to avoid re-scuffing.
symptoms: Rear window peeling or separating from top fabric
Scuff mark below the rear window glass
Water leaks / damp carpet and footwells

records.title: 3.5L V6 Coolant Crossover Tube Leak
records.description: The Chrysler 3.5L V6 engine in the Prowler uses aluminum coolant crossover tubes that develop leaks at the O-ring seals and crimped connections. The crossover tubes run across the top of the engine between the cylinder heads and are exposed to high heat. The O-rings harden and shrink, allowing coolant to seep. The Prowler's unique front-end design with exposed engine makes the leak visible but also means the engine compartment lacks the heat shielding of a conventional car.
records.solution: Replace the coolant crossover tube O-rings with Viton (fluoroelastomer) O-rings that resist heat better than the OEM rubber seals. The tubes must be removed for O-ring access. Inspect the aluminum tubes for corrosion pitting and replace if pitted. Flush the cooling system and use Mopar antifreeze/coolant. Replace the thermostat during the repair.
symptoms: Coolant dripping from top of engine
Sweet coolant smell from engine bay
Visible coolant residue on engine between cylinder heads

records.title: Overheating in Traffic Due to Limited Airflow
records.description: The Prowler's custom hot rod styling restricts airflow to the radiator, causing overheating in slow traffic or hot weather. The front-mounted radiator receives limited air through the narrow grille opening and the cooling fans may not provide adequate flow.
records.solution: Upgrade electric cooling fans to higher-CFM units. Ensure radiator is clean and not blocked by debris. Some owners add additional auxiliary fans or upgrade to an aluminum radiator for improved cooling capacity.

records.title: Door Speaker Foam Surround Deterioration
records.description: One of the three failures Prowler owners say 'will develop with every Prowler' is deterioration of the speaker foam surround (the flexible ring around the cone), starting with the door speakers first. As the foam dry-rots the speakers distort, rattle, buzz, or blow out entirely. It is a universal age-related issue on all model years, driven by the original foam-surround OEM speakers.
records.solution: Repair with a speaker re-foam kit (re-bonding a new surround to the cone) or, more commonly, replace the OEM 6-1/2 in. door speakers with aftermarket units using plastic mounting adapters to fit the Prowler's opening. Considered a minor, fully correctable issue.

records.title: Front Lower Ball Joint Separation (Safety Recall C03 / NHTSA 03V034000)
records.description: The front lower ball joints are a widely reported weak point and were the subject of Chrysler Safety Recall C03 (NHTSA campaign 03V034000). Moisture intrusion past the ball joint boot causes internal corrosion and stud wear. The joint can separate from the lower control arm (A-arm) without warning, most commonly when pulling away from a curb with the wheels turned or when driving straight at normal speed, resulting in sudden loss of steering, wheel collapse, and a crash. Because the Prowler has a low production volume and aging fleet, this remains the single most safety-critical known issue.
records.solution: Verify recall completion by VIN through Mopar/dealer; recall repair replaces the lower ball joints (recall kit) at no cost on eligible VINs. Out of warranty, inspect boots for tears and check for play by rocking the tire top-to-bottom; replace worn ball joints immediately. Aftermarket lower ball joint reference PN 13768 (Mopar recall service kit under campaign C03). Torn boots or any measurable play warrant immediate replacement.
symptoms: Sudden loss of steering when turning at low speed
Clunk or play when rocking the front tire top-to-bottom
Torn or missing lower ball joint rubber boot
Wheel collapse / vehicle drops on one corner

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 03V-034 - Prowler Front Lower Ball Joints

records.title: Fuel Gauge Reads Inaccurately / Won't Show Full (Sending Unit)
records.description: Owners commonly report the fuel gauge not reading full after fill-up or reading erratically. The in-tank fuel level sending unit (and its O-ring, shared with early Harley V-Rods) is the usual culprit, and Chrysler released a fuel-control/regulator update to address the gauge not reading full. The gauge on this platform also does not respond when the sender is moved by hand on the bench, which leads to misdiagnosis.
records.solution: Verify sender resistance with a DVOM before replacing (Full = ~950-1050 ohms, 3/4 = 800, 1/2 = 550, 1/4 = 300, Empty = 50-150 ohms). For the 'won't read full' complaint, install the released fuel control valve kit, Mopar PN 05093967AA. Replace the sending unit O-ring when the tank/pump is open. Do not judge the repair by bench-moving the sender by hand — this platform's gauge won't update that way.
symptoms: Gauge doesn't read full after fill-up
Gauge reads empty with fuel in tank

records.title: Aluminum Body Panel Paint Adhesion Failure
records.description: The Prowler uses aluminum body panels that suffer from paint adhesion issues, particularly on the fenders and hood. The aluminum surface preparation at the factory was inadequate, causing paint to bubble, flake, and peel. The problem is worse on 1999 Prowler Purple models and 2001 Orange models. Touch-up paint does not adhere to the bare aluminum without proper etching primer. The aluminum panels are also more susceptible to hail dents and parking lot dings than steel.
records.solution: Affected panels must be stripped to bare aluminum, treated with a self-etching aluminum primer, then resprayed. Body shops experienced with aluminum (Corvette/aluminum body truck shops) are recommended. Paintless dent repair is effective for minor dings on the aluminum panels. For storage, use a quality car cover to protect against UV damage to the paint and prevent further peeling.
symptoms: Paint bubbling on fenders or hood
Paint peeling in sheets from aluminum panels
Clear coat failure with chalky appearance
Paint flaking around edges of panels
Bare aluminum visible where paint has lifted

records.title: PCM Internal Checksum Failure (P0601) / Obsolete Engine Computer
records.description: The engine PCM (Powertrain Control Module) suffers an internal memory-chip failure that sets code P0601 'Internal Control Module Check-Sum Error' and illuminates the Check Engine Light, which also causes the car to fail most state inspections. If ignored, the PCM progressively degrades and can fail completely, leaving the car stranded. Because the Prowler's PCM is a low-volume, long-out-of-production unit, replacement is a documented ownership headache.
records.solution: The internal chip failure can often be repaired and re-flashed by specialists rather than scrapping the unit; owners are directed to Prowler-specific PCM repair/reprogramming services (e.g., BGPerformance) or to buy a refurbished, VIN-programmed plug-and-play PCM. Cleaning corroded PCM connector pins resolves some intermittent no-start/driveability cases before a rebuild is needed.
symptoms: Complete PCM failure leaving car stranded

records.title: In-Tank Fuel Pump Failure / No Rail Pressure (Obsolete OEM Pump)
records.description: Owners report the in-tank electric fuel pump failing, producing a crank-but-no-start or hard-hot-start condition where the pump has power but delivers no pressure to the fuel rail. The problem is compounded because the original OEM Prowler fuel pump/sending-unit assembly is no longer available and correct aftermarket assemblies are limited, making sourcing a proper replacement difficult.
records.solution: Diagnose by checking fuel pressure at the rail (power present but zero/low pressure confirms a dead pump) and rule out vacuum/air-intake leaks for hard-start cases. Repair is replacement of the in-tank fuel pump/module; because the complete OEM unit is discontinued, owners often adapt a compatible Mopar 3.5L aftermarket pump into the original hanger/basket assembly.
symptoms: No fuel pressure at the rail despite power to pump

records.title: AutoStick Transmission Harsh Shifting
records.description: The 4-speed automatic with AutoStick develops harsh and erratic shifts. The transmission adaptive learning software can become confused, and solenoid pack issues cause delayed or harsh gear changes.
records.solution: Reset transmission adaptive learning by disconnecting battery for 30 minutes. If shifts remain harsh, replace the solenoid pack and flush transmission fluid. Use only ATF+4 fluid (Mopar spec).

records.title: 42LE Automatic Transmission Overheating (Rear-Mounted)
records.description: The Prowler uses a unique rear-mounted Chrysler 42LE 4-speed automatic transaxle with the differential integrated into the unit. The transmission is mounted at the rear axle (like a Corvette) for weight distribution, but the rear mounting location receives less cooling airflow than a front-mounted transmission. Combined with the 3.5L V6's torque, the 42LE overheats during spirited driving, causing shift quality degradation and premature clutch wear. There is no factory auxiliary cooler.
records.solution: Install an auxiliary transmission cooler with a thermostat to maintain optimal temperature. Route the cooler lines to the front of the vehicle where airflow is available. Change the ATF+4 fluid every 20,000 miles — the rear-mounted transmission runs significantly hotter than a front-mounted unit. A temperature gauge adapter in the cooler line helps monitor transmission temperature. Avoid stop-and-go driving on hot days.
symptoms: Harsh or delayed shifts after extended driving
Burning ATF smell from rear of vehicle
Transmission fluid dark or burnt on dipstick
Limp mode after aggressive driving (shift to 2nd only)

records.title: A/C Condenser Leak from Road Debris Impact
records.description: The A/C condenser in the PT Cruiser is positioned close to the front of the vehicle with minimal protection from the grille, making it vulnerable to road debris impact damage. Small rocks and pebbles puncture the thin aluminum condenser tubes, causing refrigerant leaks. The condenser is also prone to corrosion, particularly in areas with road salt use. The result is a gradual or sudden loss of A/C cooling.
records.solution: Replace the A/C condenser. The condenser is accessible from the front of the vehicle after removing the front bumper cover and grille. Replace the receiver/drier at the same time (standard practice) and install a new expansion valve if the system has been open to atmosphere for an extended period. Evacuate and recharge with the correct amount of R-134a. Budget $400-$700 for parts and labor. Consider installing a small mesh screen behind the grille to protect the new condenser.
symptoms: Hissing sound from front of vehicle (active refrigerant leak)
Oily residue on condenser surface near impact points
Visible bent or punctured fins on the condenser

records.title: EGR Valve Failure and Carbon Buildup
records.description: The EGR (Exhaust Gas Recirculation) valve on the 2.4L engine clogs with carbon deposits and sticks open or closed. When stuck open, it causes rough idle, stalling, and hesitation. When stuck closed, it increases NOx emissions and may trigger a check engine light. The EGR passages in the intake manifold also clog with carbon, reducing effectiveness even with a functioning valve. The turbo model is especially prone due to higher exhaust temperatures.
records.solution: Remove the EGR valve and clean it with carburetor cleaner and a wire brush. Clean the EGR passages in the intake manifold with a long bristle brush. If the valve diaphragm is torn or the pintle is worn, replace the EGR valve (Standard Motor Products EGV880 or equivalent). Also clean the EGR tube connecting the exhaust manifold to the valve. Budget $150-$400 for cleaning and/or replacement.
symptoms: Rough idle or stalling at idle
Check engine light with EGR flow codes
Failed emissions test for high NOx
Engine surging or hunting at idle

records.title: Head Gasket Failure (Especially Turbo Models)
records.description: Head gasket failure is common, especially on turbo models. The aluminum cylinder head is susceptible to pitting from acidic coolant which compromises the gasket seal. Turbo models experience higher cylinder pressures that accelerate failure. Overheating from cooling system issues frequently triggers head gasket failure.
records.solution: Replace head gasket with Fel-Pro MLS gasket. HS 9946 PT for 2001, HS26206PT-1 for 2002-2009, or individual gasket 26206PT for 2002-2010. Machine cylinder head surface if pitting present. Replace thermostat and flush cooling system. Check head for warpage before reinstalling.
symptoms: White smoke from exhaust (coolant entering combustion)
Coolant loss with no visible external leak
Milky residue on oil cap (coolant in oil)

records.title: Engine Oil Sludge Buildup (2.4L Non-Turbo)
records.description: The 2.4L DOHC non-turbo engine in the PT Cruiser is highly susceptible to oil sludge formation, particularly when oil changes are delayed beyond 3,000-5,000 miles or conventional oil is used. The engine design with its small oil passages and relatively high operating temperature creates ideal conditions for sludge. Sludge clogs oil passages, starving the valvetrain and camshaft bearings of lubrication, leading to ticking noises and eventual engine damage.
records.solution: Switch to full synthetic 5W-30 oil and change every 5,000 miles maximum. For engines with existing sludge, perform 3 consecutive oil changes at 1,000-mile intervals using synthetic oil to flush deposits. In severe cases where the engine is ticking, a manual cleaning may be needed — remove the valve cover and manually clean sludge from the cam journals and oil passages. If cam bearings are damaged from oil starvation, engine replacement may be needed ($2,000-$4,000).
symptoms: Engine ticking or tapping noise, especially on cold start
Oil pressure warning light flickering at idle
Dark, thick sludge visible on oil filler cap or dipstick
Check engine light with cam timing or oil pressure codes

records.title: Chronic Overheating - Multiple Causes
records.description: PT Cruisers are extremely prone to overheating from multiple causes: radiator fan relay failure, fan motor failure, thermostat sticking closed, radiator clogging, and water pump failure. The high-speed fan relay is the most frequent single failure point. Overheating leads to head gasket failure. This is one of the most universally reported problems across all model years.
records.solution: Diagnose root cause systematically: check fan relay (5149541AA) first, then fan motor, thermostat (Stant 45359), water pump, and radiator. Replace radiator cap (frequently causes overpressure issues). Cooling fan module 5017407AB for complete fan assembly replacement.
symptoms: Temperature gauge climbing above normal, especially at idle
A/C compressor disengaging (safety cutoff from high temps)
Radiator fan not running with engine hot
Steam or coolant smell from engine bay
Check engine light with coolant temp codes

records.title: Timing Belt Failure - Critical on Turbo Models
records.description: The 2.4L DOHC engine requires timing belt replacement at 60,000-90,000 mile intervals. The non-turbo version is non-interference (belt failure won't destroy engine), but the turbo GT version IS an interference engine where timing belt failure causes catastrophic valve-to-piston contact and engine destruction. Water pump is driven by timing belt and must be replaced simultaneously. Job rates 8/10 difficulty due to extremely tight engine bay.
records.solution: Replace timing belt, water pump, tensioner, and idler pulleys as a complete kit. Gates PowerGrip Timing Belt Kit with water pump TCKWP265C (2003-2009) or TCKWP265B (2001-2002). Mopar water pump 4694307AB. Labor is 6-8 hours due to tight engine bay. NEVER skip on turbo models.
symptoms: Ticking or slapping noise from timing cover area
Engine cranks but won't start (belt jumped)

records.title: Turbocharger Failure (GT/Turbo Models)
records.description: The turbocharger on GT and turbo models fails from oil starvation, wastegate actuator failure, and bearing wear. Failures reported as early as 60,000-78,000 miles. Turbo failure is often followed by head gasket failure within months due to changes in combustion pressure dynamics.
records.solution: Replace turbocharger assembly (Mopar 4884183AD) and turbo oil feed line (4891252AA). Must address root cause: oil feed line restriction, wastegate failure. Replace oil feed and drain lines during turbo replacement. Use only full synthetic oil and change every 3,000 miles. Idle 30-60 seconds before shutdown to cool turbo.
symptoms: Blue or white smoke from exhaust under acceleration
Whining or grinding noise from turbo area
Check engine light with boost pressure codes

records.title: 2.7L V6 Engine Oil Sludge and Premature Failure
records.description: The 2.7L V6 engine is highly susceptible to oil sludge buildup due to higher than average operating temperatures, insufficient oil capacity (5 quarts instead of 6), and a timing chain-driven water pump that can leak coolant into the crankcase. Engine failures have been reported as early as 20,000 miles, but most commonly occur between 50,000 and 60,000 miles. Multiple class action lawsuits were filed.
records.solution: Prevention requires strict oil change intervals of 3,000 miles or less with high-quality synthetic oil. Once sludge has formed, engine flush treatments may help in early stages. Severe cases require timing chain replacement ($1,289-$1,642) or complete engine replacement ($3,500-$6,000).

records.title: 3.5L V6 Head Gasket Failure and Overheating
records.description: The 3.5L V6 engine has common issues including leaky head gaskets, coolant leaks, and overheating. The water pump uses a molded plastic impeller that erodes from rust and sediment in the coolant, reducing cooling efficiency. These engines run hot and are prone to oil sludging, especially if oil is not changed every 3,000 miles.
records.solution: Water pump and thermostat replacement together costs $400-$700 and should be done at the first sign of overheating. Head gasket replacement is a major repair costing $1,925-$2,512. Regular cooling system maintenance including coolant flushes every 30,000 miles can prevent many issues.
symptoms: Coolant loss with no visible leak
Rough idle when engine is cold

records.title: Alternator and PCM-Integrated Voltage Regulator Failure
records.description: The Sebring's voltage regulator is integrated into the PCM (Powertrain Control Module), not the alternator. This unusual design means a voltage regulator failure requires PCM diagnosis/replacement rather than simple alternator work. Alternators also fail prematurely around 70,000 miles. Ground corrosion and battery terminal strip issues compound the problem.
records.solution: Test alternator output and PCM voltage regulator function separately. Replace alternator (Remy Remanufactured 12423 for 2.7L) if output is low. If alternator tests good, PCM voltage regulator circuit has failed. Clean all battery terminals and ground connections, especially under PCM. External voltage regulator conversion available for chronic cases.
symptoms: Vehicle stalling due to low voltage

records.title: Convertible Top Water Leaks and Drainage Issues
records.description: Convertible models are prone to multiple water leak issues. The rear window can separate from the convertible top fabric as the top shrinks with age. The drain system below the convertible top can become clogged, causing water to back up into the rocker panels and interior. Weatherstripping failure and clogged windshield channels also contribute to leaks.
records.solution: Regular maintenance of drain holes (located in seams under the doors) can prevent backup issues - clean with compressed air or flexible wire ($0 DIY). Weatherstrip replacement costs $50-$200. Complete convertible top replacement costs $800-$2,500 for aftermarket tops or $2,000-$4,000 for OEM with professional installation.
symptoms: Water pooling on floorboards after rain
Wet carpet in trunk or rear storage area
Musty or mold smell in interior
Visible gap between rear window and top fabric

records.title: Front Suspension Control Arm and Bushing Wear
records.description: The front suspension control arms and bushings are prone to premature wear, with over 45 reported problems specifically related to front suspension control arms. Ball joints rust and require replacement, and control arms can become loose over time. Worn control arm bushings cause squeaking sounds over bumps, and severe wear results in knocking sounds.
records.solution: Control arm bushing replacement alone costs $255-$306. Complete control arm replacement costs $951-$1,043. Strut and shock replacement costs $541-$632. A full front suspension rebuild including control arms, ball joints, struts, and alignment can cost $1,500-$2,500.
symptoms: Knocking or clunking from front end

records.title: 2.7L V6 Timing Chain Stretch and Internal Water Pump Seizure
records.description: The 2.7L V6 uses a timing chain that stretches prematurely due to oil sludge buildup restricting lubrication. The chain-driven internal water pump can seize and cause the timing chain to jump, destroying the engine. Water pump, timing chain, guides, and tensioner are all internal components requiring extensive disassembly to access. 7-8 hours labor.
records.solution: Replace timing chain kit (Mopar 68036787AA, updated design), water pump (Mopar 4892425AA - MUST use Mopar updated design, NOT aftermarket), all guides, tensioner, and seals as a complete job. Preventive maintenance at 100,000 miles. Always replace water pump with timing chain.
symptoms: Rattling noise from engine on startup
Check engine light with timing codes
Complete engine failure if chain jumps

records.title: TIPM (Totally Integrated Power Module) Failure
records.description: The Totally Integrated Power Module (TIPM), located in the engine compartment near the air cleaner assembly, houses all important fuses and power relays. Water intrusion into the module can cause corrosion and electrical system failures. The TIPM controls critical systems including fuel pump operation, headlights, airbags, door locks, and air conditioning.
records.solution: TIPM repair services can rebuild the unit for $200-$400, which is more cost-effective than purchasing a new OEM TIPM ($600-$1,200 for parts plus $100-$200 labor for programming and installation). Address any water intrusion issues by checking seals and drainage.
symptoms: Fuel pump not activating (engine cranks but won't start)

records.title: Automatic Transmission Slipping and Shifting Problems
records.description: The A604 (41TE) transmission used in 2001-2006 models and the 62TE 6-speed transmission in 2007-2010 models are prone to slipping between gears, hard shifts, and delayed engagement. The A604 has known OE design flaws, while the 62TE commonly experiences solenoid pack failures.
records.solution: For minor shifting issues, a transmission fluid and filter change may help ($150-$300). Solenoid pack replacement costs $400-$800. For severe issues, a transmission rebuild costs $1,800-$3,500, while a complete replacement costs $2,500-$4,500.
symptoms: Delayed engagement into Drive or Reverse
Failure to upshift at highway speeds
Stalling when coming to a stop

records.title: Power Window Regulator and Motor Failure
records.description: Power window regulators and motors are a common failure point across all Sebring body styles. The cable-style regulators are prone to plastic component breakage, causing the metal cable to become loose and the window to fall into the door. Cable grooves wear over time, causing frayed cables that tangle and bunch up. Window motors can also burn out from strain.
records.solution: Window regulator replacement with motor costs $227-$310 on average. Complete window regulator assemblies that include the motor are available and often recommended over repairing individual components. Labor costs are typically 1-2 hours.
symptoms: Window tilts when going up or down
Window won't go up or down at all

records.title: 62TE Transmission Solenoid Pack Failure
records.description: The 62TE 6-speed automatic transmission experiences solenoid pack failures causing hard shifting, slipping, limp mode (stuck in 3rd gear), and complete transmission failure. The solenoid pack contains 6 shift solenoids, 1 line-pressure solenoid, a temperature sensor, and 5 pressure switches. Most frequent in 2012 and 2014 models.
records.solution: Start with solenoid pack replacement (68376696AA or 5078709AB). If internal damage present, full transmission rebuild ($2,500-$4,500). Always use ONLY Mopar ATF+4 fluid (68218058AC). Change fluid every 30,000 miles despite Chrysler's lifetime claim.
symptoms: Delayed engagement from Park to Drive

records.title: Cooling System Failures (3.3L/3.8L V6)
records.description: The 3.3L and 3.8L V6 engines suffer from water pump failures, thermostat failures, and radiator fan relay failures. The water pump weep hole is a common leak point. Overheating can cause head gasket failure. The cooling fan relay is a frequent failure point causing overheating at idle.
records.solution: Replace water pump (Gates 43090 for 3.8L), thermostat (Stant 45359, 195F), and radiator cap as a set. Check cooling fan relay in fuse box. Flush entire cooling system with Mopar OAT coolant (68048953AB). Monitor temperature gauge regularly, especially in summer traffic.
symptoms: Engine overheating, especially at idle or in traffic
Coolant leak from water pump area
Radiator fan not running at idle

records.title: Ignition Switch and SKREEM Module Failure
records.description: The ignition switch and SKREEM (Sentry Key Remote Entry Module) fail, preventing the vehicle from starting or causing intermittent no-start conditions. The SKREEM module reads the transponder in the key and communicates with the PCM. Failure causes 'no bus' communication errors.
records.solution: Replace ignition switch (Mopar 4685863AH) and/or SKREEM module (Mopar 56046149AE). New keys may need to be programmed at dealer. Try cleaning key and ignition cylinder first - cleaning the key transponder ring around the ignition cylinder resolves intermittent issues for some owners.
symptoms: Intermittent no-start that resolves after waiting

records.title: Power Sliding Door Cable and Motor Failure
records.description: Power sliding doors fail to open or close automatically, open partially and stop, or operate intermittently. The drive cable, motor, and lock actuator are common failure points. Insulation wear in wiring harness causes shorts. Chrysler issued a campaign for harness chafing on 2008-2009 builds. Class-action lawsuit covers 2013-2016 models.
records.solution: Replace drive cable assembly (cable not serviced separately). Left side: 68064661AE (updated part), right side: 68064660AC. Replace lock actuator if door won't latch (left: 5020679AB, right: 5020678AA). Check wiring harness for chafing, especially on 2008-2009 models. Track motor: 68067847AF.
symptoms: Sliding door opens partially then stops
Door motor makes noise but door doesn't move
Door Ajar warning despite door being closed
Door won't latch or unlatch electrically

records.title: TIPM (Totally Integrated Power Module) Failure
records.description: The TIPM central fuse/relay box controls nearly all vehicle electrical functions. Internal relays, especially the fuel pump relay, fail due to solder joint cracking from thermal cycling. Causes random activation of lights, wipers, horn, sliding doors losing power, battery drain, and no-start conditions. Class-action lawsuit filed. Most severe in 2008 and 2010-2011 model years.
records.solution: Three options: (1) New TIPM from dealer ($800-$1,500 + programming), (2) Mail-in TIPM rebuild service from UpFix, Circuit Board Medics, or MAKS TIPM ($200-$400, plug-and-play, no programming needed), (3) External fuel pump relay bypass cable ($50-$150) for fuel pump relay issue only.
symptoms: Vehicle won't start (fuel pump relay failure)
Fuel pump runs continuously with key off
Wipers, horn, or lights activate randomly
Power sliding doors lose power mid-operation
Battery drain from interior lights activating overnight

records.title: 3.6L Pentastar V6 Oil Filter Housing / Oil Cooler Assembly Cracking (Oil & Coolant Leaks)
records.description: The Voyager's 3.6L Pentastar V6 uses a plastic oil filter housing that integrates the engine oil cooler, where hot oil is cooled by engine coolant. The plastic housing and its internal O-rings/gaskets become brittle from constant underhood heat cycling and crack or warp over time, producing simultaneous oil and coolant leaks. Because oil and coolant passages are adjacent inside the unit, a failure can allow coolant-oil cross-contamination. This is one of the most widely documented Pentastar defects across the Pacifica/Voyager/Grand Caravan/Durango/Grand Cherokee family. Owners typically notice it after 60,000-100,000 miles, though earlier failures occur if the oil filter cap is overtightened. Chrysler has never issued a recall for it.
records.solution: Replace the oil filter housing / oil cooler assembly along with the O-rings and gaskets. The commonly preferred fix is an aftermarket aluminum housing (e.g., Dorman) rather than the original plastic unit, which resists heat-related cracking and helps prevent recurrence. Coolant and oil are drained/refilled as part of the job. Torque the filter cap to spec (do not overtighten) to avoid cracking the replacement.
symptoms: Oil leak / oil spots under front of engine
Coolant leak and dropping coolant level
Burning oil smell from engine bay
Oil or coolant pooling near the oil filter housing (top/front of engine)
Low oil pressure warning if leak is severe

records.title: 3.6L Pentastar Valvetrain Failure (Rocker Arm / Lifter Ticking, Misfire, Engine Damage)
records.description: The 3.6L Pentastar V6 has a documented valvetrain defect involving the rocker arms and their roller lift pins and the associated hydraulic lifters. The roller on a rocker arm can prematurely wear, loosen and drop, shifting the rocker out of alignment so it scrapes the camshaft and generates metal debris that contaminates the oil and circulates through the engine. Symptoms include a persistent ticking/tapping noise, misfires, hesitation/bucking, rough running and loss of power, and in severe cases catastrophic engine failure requiring a full engine replacement. A proposed class action against FCA US alleges the automaker knew of the valve-train defect in 2014-2020 model year vehicles (which includes the 2020 launch year of the modern Voyager); ECM software governing lifter timing was also implicated.
records.solution: Diagnose the failing cylinder(s) via misfire codes and cylinder-specific inspection. Accepted repair is replacement of the affected rocker arm(s) and lifter(s); if debris has circulated or multiple cylinders are affected, a cylinder head or full engine replacement may be required. Apply any applicable PCM/ECM software update. Frequent oil changes with correct-spec oil and not deferring the ticking noise limit collateral damage.
symptoms: Ticking or tapping noise from the engine (often at idle/cold start)

records.title: 948TE 9-Speed Transmission Calibration Issues
records.description: The 948TE 9-speed automatic paired with the 3.6L Pentastar V6 has well-documented calibration issues. Hesitation during light-throttle acceleration, delayed 2nd-to-3rd upshifts, and shuddering under load. For 2023+, Chrysler introduced revised valve body and updated shift logic with fewer complaints.
records.solution: Get latest PCM/TCM software update from dealer (often resolves 80%+ of shifting complaints). For 2020-2022, updated 2023 valve body can be installed. Regular transmission fluid service every 60,000 miles.
symptoms: Shuddering under load at low speeds
Occasional clunk when shifting from Park

records.title: Rear HVAC Blower Motor Resistor Failure
records.description: The rear HVAC blower motor resistor fails, causing the rear fan to work only on highest speed setting or not at all. Particularly problematic in a minivan where rear passengers rely on rear climate control.
records.solution: Replace rear blower motor resistor (Mopar 68233575AA). Accessible from behind rear interior trim. Easy DIY repair in 30-60 minutes. Check for debris blocking rear air intake before replacing resistor.
symptoms: Rear fan works only on highest speed
Burning smell from rear HVAC vent area

records.title: Second-Row Seat-to-Floor Latch May Bind Open (LATCH/FMVSS 225 Recall Z22 / 22V-181)
records.description: On 2021 Voyager (and 2021-2022 Pacifica) vehicles equipped with Easy Slide second-row bucket seats (sales code CY3), the second-row seat-to-floor mounting latch can bind and stick in the open position, so the seat does not properly secure to the floor and fails the lateral-force requirement of FMVSS No. 225 (Child Restraint Anchorage Systems). This means a child seat installed via LATCH may not be safely anchored. Recall Z22 (NHTSA 22V-181) covered roughly 1,160 vehicles (1,094 Pacifica, 66 Voyager) built October 4-28, 2021.
records.solution: Free safety recall (Stellantis Z22 / NHTSA 22V-181). Dealers inspect the second-row seat-to-floor latch and, if necessary, replace the second-row seat cushion frame so the seat latches and secures properly. Owners can verify by VIN and have the repair done at no charge.
symptoms: Second-row seat does not lock/secure firmly to the floor
Seat latch feels stuck or stays open
Seat rocks or is loose when installed
Difficulty getting a secure child-seat LATCH anchor

records.title: Side Curtain Airbag Defects (May Not Deploy / Insufficient Pressure) - Safety Recalls
records.description: The Voyager is covered by two separate NHTSA side-curtain airbag recalls. In the first (2020-2023 Voyager/Pacifica), a side curtain airbag electrical connector that was not properly secured may prevent the airbags from deploying in a crash (only about 3 Voyagers plus ~23 Pacificas). In the later, much larger recall (NHTSA 26V-189 / Stellantis 06D, ~253,000 MY2022-2026 Pacifica and Voyager, of which ~23,879 are Voyagers), the left and/or right side curtain airbags have improperly sealed seams so they cannot retain sufficient pressure during a side-impact deployment (a noncompliance with FMVSS 226). Both defects reduce occupant protection in a side crash.
records.solution: Both are free safety recalls. Dealers inspect and, as needed, properly secure the side curtain airbag connector (connector recall) or replace one or both side curtain airbags (sealing recall 06D / 26V-189). Owners should check their VIN at NHTSA.gov or mopar.com/recalls and schedule the recall service at no cost.
symptoms: No symptoms until a side-impact crash where the airbag fails to deploy or under-inflates

records.title: Power Sliding Door Malfunction
records.description: The power sliding doors fail to open, close, or reverse direction unexpectedly mid-travel. The door latch sensor, track motor, and wiring harness in the door jamb are common failure points on the budget-oriented Voyager.
records.solution: Diagnose the specific failure point: latch mechanism (Dorman 940-100), track motor, or wiring. The flex wire harness in the door jamb breaks from constant flexing. Reset by disconnecting battery for 5 minutes and recalibrating door.

records.title: UConnect 4 Touchscreen Delamination
records.description: The UConnect 4 7-inch infotainment touchscreen suffers from capacitive layer delamination, especially near the bottom third. Screen becomes unresponsive in affected areas, requiring physical replacement. Same unit used in the Pacifica. Hardware defect with no software fix available.
records.solution: Screen replacement at dealer. No software fix available as this is a hardware defect. Check if still under warranty before paying. Some owners use screen protectors to slow the delamination process.
symptoms: Visible discoloration or separation of screen layers
Screen requires harder presses to register

records.title: Windshield Wiper Arm Nuts Improperly Tightened (Wiper Failure Recall Z80 / 22V-619)
records.description: Certain 2022 Chrysler Voyager and Pacifica minivans left the factory with windshield wiper arm retaining nuts that were not torqued to specification. A loose nut allows the wiper arm to slip on its spline, so one or both wipers stop clearing the windshield properly or fail to operate, creating a loss of forward visibility (especially in rain/snow) and a crash risk that can occur without prior warning. The recall (Stellantis Z80 / NHTSA 22V-619) covered 508 units total (456 Pacifica, 52 Voyager) built November 26 - December 23, 2021.
records.solution: Free safety recall (NHTSA 22V-619 / Stellantis Z80). Dealers inspect and tighten the windshield wiper arm retaining nuts to the correct torque (about a 30-minute repair). If a wiper arm was already damaged by running loose, it is replaced. Owners can check their VIN and schedule the repair at no charge.
symptoms: Wiper arm does not clear the windshield properly
Wipers not parking/resting in correct position
Wiper arm slips or flops loosely
Reduced visibility in rain or snow
